items.title: Algérie : qui est Adil Bourabaa, la surprise de Hemdani pour remplacer Bentaleb ?
items.description: Le milieu de terrain de l'équipe d'Algérie de football, Nabil Bentaleb , s'est blessé dimanche soir avec son club de Lille en championnat de France. Pour le remplacer, le sélectionneur Brahim Hemdani a fait appel à un nouveau nom, Adil Bourabaa, sociétaire de Le Mans FC. Outre ses qualités avérées, le joueur répond au critère fixé par le nouveau sélectionneur, qui est de jouer en club et d'être en forme. Convoqué chez les U23, Adil Bourabaa se retrouve chez les A Bentaleb, devenu une pièce maîtresse du milieu de terrain des Verts depuis son retour à la compétition en février 2025 après son malaise cardiaque, figurait parmi les six milieux convoqués par Hemdani pour le stage de ce mois de septembre. Mais le joueur a contracté une blessure dimanche soir lors du match Nice-Lille (2-1). L’Algérien a quitté le terrain à la 77ᵉ minute. Ce lundi, la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF) a annoncé que Nabil Bentaleb est forfait pour les deux prochains matchs des Verts face à la Zambie le 25 septembre à Tizi-Ouzou et au Burundi le 29 septembre à Bujumbura. L’instance fédérale a aussi annoncé le nom du remplaçant du Lillois. Il s’agit du milieu du Mans, Adil Bourabaa. Celui-ci était initialement convoqué par Rafik Saïfi chez les U23 avant de finalement constituer une solution pour Brahim Hemdani. Né en 2005 à Drancy (France), Adil Bourabaa a fait ses débuts à Guingamp puis à Leganés, en Espagne. En seniors, il a évolué chez Troyes et Beauvais avant de signer cette année chez Le Mans FC. Dans ce club, le joueur a fait une progression fulgurante. L’un des joueurs les plus décisifs du championnat de France Lors de sa première conférence de presse jeudi dernier, Brahim Hemdani a expliqué que son critère principal de sélection est la forme du moment de chaque joueur. Dans ce registre, il faut dire que Bourabaa fait très fort actuellement. Son début de saison est tonitruant. Depuis le début de cet exercice 2026-2027, il a pris part comme titulaire aux cinq matchs de son équipe, présentant un bilan impressionnant : 100 % de titularisations, participation à 88 % du temps de jeu et contribution à 56 % des buts de son équipe. En cinq rencontres de Ligue 1 française, il a inscrit trois buts et a délivré deux passes décisives. Pour un milieu de terrain, il est difficile de faire mieux. Les commentateurs le désignent comme l’un des joueurs les plus décisifs de ce début de saison en France. L’ascension fulgurante de Adil Bourabaa La progression de Adil Bourabaa est aussi impressionnante. En janvier dernier, il végétait dans les profondeurs des divisions inférieures, chez Beauvais, en régionale 2. Il a été transféré au Mans en février pour la modique somme de 15.000 euros. Huit mois après, il est l’un des hommes en forme du championnat de l'élite avec à la clé une place chez une sélection mondialiste. Sa valeur marchande est passée à 500.000 euros selon le site Transfermarkt, et ce n'est que le début. Pour l'Algérie et Brahim Hemdani, il s’agit d'une excellente trouvaille. En plus d'être en forme, Bourabaa est aussi jeune (21 ans) et polyvalent, pouvant jouer comme milieu central, milieu droit et arrière-droit. Il pourrait valoir des satisfactions aux Verts dans les années à venir, et peut-être même dans l’immédiat. L’article Algérie : qui est Adil Bourabaa, la surprise de Hemdani pour remplacer Bentaleb ? est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Burkina : « Jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les lauréates du concours « Hakili Mousso »
items.description: (Ouagadougou, 21 septembre 2026). Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a reçu ce lundi en audience, les lauréates du concours de détection de talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso », conduite par la Ministre Conseillère spéciale du Président du Faso, chargée du Développement technologique, la Camarade Dr Floriane OUÉDRAOGO/ZONGO. Ce lundi 21 septembre était « jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les filles lauréates du concours national de détection des talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso » et les meilleurs enseignants dans les disciplines scientifiques. Dans cette “salle de classe” d’une heure, ils ont eu droit à une master class du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, sur l’importance des disciplines scientifiques dans le développement. Outre les félicitations pour leur esprit d’abnégation, de surpassement de soi, le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire a prodigué des conseils aux lauréates. Il s’agit entre autres de l’amour des métiers scientifiques, du travail, de la confiance en soi. « Ne vous fixez-pas de limites. Vous êtes capables de tout faire. (…) Demain, nous attendons de vous des ingénieurs en mécanique, mécatronique, électronique, en physique, en astrologie. Vous devez vous donner des objectifs et les atteindre », a dit le Chef de l’État. HAKILI Mousso, un creuset pour l’éclosion d’une élite féminine Le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, a rappelé que le Concours « HAKILI Mousso » ne s’inscrit pas dans la politique du genre importée par les impérialistes avec le dessein d’opposer les femmes aux hommes. « Nous nous inscrivons dans une politique d’élite. Encourager les femmes vers certains métiers qui nous intéressent », a indiqué le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Au cours de cette audience, le Président du Faso a réitéré son engagement pour le développement du Burkina Faso dont la clé de voûte repose sur la qualité des ressources humaines. La première en chimie à « HAKILI Mousso », Inès Marie Fabiolas NIKIEMA est ressortie bien confiante de l’entretien avec le Chef de l’État. Celle qui rêve de faire carrière dans l’aéronautique pour participer à développer son pays, a pris l’engagement de bien travailler et afin d’être un modèle pour les autres jeunes. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso Minute.bf

items.title: NLC demands independent investigation into death of 37 mines
items.description: The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has demanded a thorough, transparent and independent investigation into the deaths of 37 persons in NSCDC custody. NLC President, Mr Joe Ajaero, made the demand in a statement issued on Monday in Abuja, while calling for accountability and justice over the deaths. Ajaero said the victims were arrested during operations against suspected illegal mining in Niger on Sept. 15 and 16. He said the arrests occurred in the M.I. Wushishi and Lukoto areas of Niger, while the deaths were recorded on Sept. 17. “Reports indicate that many of those who died were young people, including minors,” Ajaero said. He said the Federal Government had constituted an independent committee to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths. “The committee is expected to establish the identities of the deceased, circumstances of their arrest and detention, and the cause of their deaths,” he said. Ajaero welcomed the suspension of officers connected with the incident but stressed that the measure must not replace accountability and justice. He said the NLC mourned the victims and commiserated with the Government and people of Niger over the deaths. The NLC president attributed participation in artisanal mining and other vulnerable informal activities to poverty, unemployment, deprivation and lack of decent livelihood opportunities. “These were children and young people from working-class and peasant families, particularly families whose livelihoods depend on the informal economy,” Ajaero said. He called for stronger regulation of artisanal and small-scale mining, enforcement of occupational safety standards and prohibition of hazardous child labour. Ajaero also urged government to remove children from hazardous mining activities and provide affected families with education, skills development, social protection and alternative livelihoods. He called for measures to address rural poverty, youth unemployment, lack of decent work and inadequate social protection. “We cannot continue to address the symptoms of these problems while ignoring their underlying causes.” The post NLC demands independent investigation into death of 37 mines appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs4.61 per litre, reduces HSD rate by Rs1.96
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday hiked the price of petrol by Rs4.61 per litre, but slashed that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.96 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs393.75 per litre while HSD will cost Rs422.08 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for Sept 22 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Full list: Countries exempt from UK Student visa proof of funds
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The UK has listed 63 countries and territories whose citizens do not have to prove they have enough money to support themselves when applying for a Student visa, under the UK’s “differential evidence requirement”. The exemption applies to the financial requirement for living costs, according to the UK government’s official Student visa guidance. Applicants must still meet the other requirements for the visa, including having enough money to pay for their course where applicable. The UK government said applicants from the listed countries and territories may still be asked to provide financial evidence before a decision is made on their application. If evidence is required, UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) will contact the applicant after the application has been submitted. According to the UK government, the countries and territories covered by the differential evidence requirement are: Australia Austria Bahrain Barbados Belgium Botswana Brazil Brunei Bulgaria Cambodia Canada Chile China Croatia Republic of Cyprus Czechia Denmark Dominican Republic Estonia Finland France Germany Greece Hong Kong Hungary Iceland Indonesia Ireland Italy Japan Kazakhstan Kuwait Latvia Liechtenstein Lithuania Luxembourg Macao Malaysia Malta Mauritius Mexico Netherlands New Zealand Norway Oman Peru Poland Portugal Qatar Romania Serbia Singapore Slovakia Slovenia South Korea Spain Sweden Switzerland Taiwan Thailand Tunisia United Arab Emirates United States of America The UK guidance also includes British nationals overseas among those who do not need to prove they have enough money to support themselves under this provision. How much money do other Student visa applicants need? Applicants who are required to meet the financial requirement must generally show that they have enough money to support themselves in the UK. For courses in London, the requirement is £1,529 per month for up to nine months while for courses outside London, the requirement is £1,171 per month for up to nine months. The money must generally have been held for at least 28 consecutive days, with the end of that 28-day period falling within 31 days of the visa application date. Students may also need to show enough money to pay their course fees for one academic year, up to nine months. The amount is stated on their Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). There are other circumstances in which an applicant does not have to prove the financial requirement. These include applicants who have been living in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months before applying for a Student visa, and those applying as student union sabbatical officers. Vanguard News The post Full list: Countries exempt from UK Student visa proof of funds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Lutte contre le trafic de drogue | Sept suspects arrêtés à Tunis
items.description: Une opération sécuritaire ciblant plusieurs quartiers populaires de Tunis, notamment Ezzouhour, Zahrouni, Mellassine et la cité Helal ont permis l'arrestation de sept individus recherchés pour trafic de drogues. L'opération s'est également soldée par la saisie de diverses quantités de drogues, comprenant de la cocaïne, du cannabis ainsi que des comprimés psychotropes de type « Lyrica », indique Mosaïque FM, citant une source sécuritaire, ce lundi 21 septembre 2026. Outre les stupéfiants, les forces de l'ordre ont confisqué des sommes d'argent issues de ces activités illicites ainsi que plusieurs armes blanches utilisées par les suspects. Ces derniers ont été placés en détention pour la suite des procédures. Y. N. L’article Lutte contre le trafic de drogue | Sept suspects arrêtés à Tunis est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Carrière Centre : un homme retrouvé mort après avoir vomi du sang
items.description: Un homme, présenté comme un ressortissant de Hérémakono, a été retrouvé mort ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 dans le secteur Bambou, à Carrière Centre, dans la commune de Matam. Les faits se sont produits aux environs de 13h30-14h, alors que l’homme transportait des ordures dans le secteur. Selon Zeinab Sylla, une riveraine, elle a découvert l’homme alors qu’elle sortait de la cour de sa grand-mère.D’après elle, l’homme aurait ensuite été interrogé par des personnes présentes sur les lieux pour savoir s’il avait été victime d’une agression. Il aurait répondu par la négative: «Je suis sortie de la cour de la grand-mère et j’ai trouvé ce monsieur en train de vomir du sang. J’ai appelé au secours, mais personne n’a osé s’approcher de lui. Quelqu’un lui a demandé s’il a été battu, il a répondu non. C’est ainsi qu’il s’est traîné d’un côté et j’ai vu qu’il était sur le point de rendre l’âme » témoignage Zeinab Sylla. Alertés, des riverains et les responsables locaux se sont rendus sur place. Un drap a été déposé sur le corps en attendant l’arrivée des services compétents. «On a alerté les gens, y compris le chef de quartier. On a envoyé le drap qui a été étalé sur lui », ajoute-t-elle. Diaby Mohamed, chargé à l’assainissement et au dégagement au sein du bureau de Carrière Centre, explique avoir été alerté alors qu’il revenait de la mosquée:«Après la prière de 14h, je sortais de la mosquée vers les 13h40. C’est 13h50 comme ça, j’ai vu un regroupement en haut ici. Donc, j’ai pris patience d’abord pour voir ce qui n’allait pas. Maintenant, il y a des citoyens qui sont descendus. Ils m’ont vu directement et ils m’ont dit qu’il y a un corps sans vie en haut », raconte-t-il. Selon les informations recueillies par les responsables locaux, l’homme aurait indiqué, avant son décès, qu’il venait de Hérémakono. Il aurait également cité le nom d’un certain Bangoura, présenté comme son frère et susceptible de permettre son identification. « Il a parlé d’un gars qui vit à Hermakonon qui peut le reconnaître, que c’est son frère », explique Diaby Mohamed. Des démarches ont alors été entreprises auprès des deux secteurs de Hérémakono, notamment Hérémakono Mosquée et Hérémakono Permanence, afin de retrouver cette personne et procéder à l’identification de la victime:«Eux sont venus pour l’identification, malheureusement ils n’ont pas pu l’identifier. Donc ce monsieur dont il a parlé, on n’a pas pu retrouver ce monsieur Bangoura jusqu’à présent », précise-t-il. Après la découverte du corps, les responsables du quartier ont alerté les services de sécurité afin de suivre la procédure prévue en pareille circonstance:«Nous avons déjà conservé son intégrité, c’est-à-dire mettre une couverture sur lui. Maintenant, nous avons dit de passer aux procédures normales, nous avons appelé au Central, puis à la gendarmerie. Ceux-ci se sont déplacés directement, venus sur les lieux », indique Diaby Mohamed. Le commissariat central ainsi que la Police technique et scientifique se sont rendus sur place pour effectuer les constatations nécessaires. Pour l’heure, l’identité officielle de la victime n’a pas encore été établie. Une hypothèse médicale évoquant une tuberculose aurait été avancée à partir de l’examen physique, mais la cause exacte du décès reste à confirmer par les services compétents. Les circonstances précises de cette mort survenue en pleine journée dans le secteur Bambou restent donc à établir. Mayi Cissé L’article Carrière Centre : un homme retrouvé mort après avoir vomi du sang est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Mbour : dix personnes interpellées après une sortie non autorisée du Kankourang
items.description: Dix personnes ont été interpellées à Mbour par la Sûreté urbaine du Commissariat central, avec le renfort d’éléments du GMI et de la BIP, pour avoir organisé une sortie du Kankourang en dehors du cadre fixé par les autorités. L’opération a ciblé plusieurs cellules culturelles communément appelées « lël », qui auraient fait sortir le Kankourang alors qu’elles ne figuraient pas parmi les entités autorisées par l’arrêté préfectoral du 28 août 2026 encadrant les festivités du « Septembre mandingue ». Selon les forces de sécurité, les groupes concernés avaient été informés des dispositions en vigueur et conviés à une réunion d’information organisée par la police. Malgré ces rappels, ils auraient maintenu leurs activités. Les interventions menées dans différents « lël » ont également permis, selon la police, de saisir sept machettes, quatre tambours traditionnels ainsi qu’un cornet de chanvre indien retrouvé en possession de l’un des mis en cause. Les dix suspects ont été placés en garde à vue avant d’être déférés devant le procureur de la République près le Tribunal de grande instance de Mbour. Ils devront répondre notamment de non-respect d’une mesure administrative, de participation à une manifestation interdite, de trouble à l’ordre public et de détention d’arme blanche. Le dispositif préfectoral autorise la sortie du Kankourang pour huit cellules : Thiocé Ouest, Santesou, Thiocé Est, Sadio Kunda, Woyinka, Juju Cissé Kunda, Diamagueune et Kuyamba.

items.title: Coopération nigéro algérienne : Mohamed Arkab à Niamey pour accélérer le TSGP et le chantier de Kafra…
items.description: Le ministre d’État algérien des Hydrocarbures, Mohamed Arkab, est arrivé cet après-midi à Niamey pour une visite de travail de deux jours. Cette visite s’effectue sur instructions du président de la République algérienne, Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Il a été accueilli à l’aéroport par le ministre nigérien du Pétrole, Hamadou Tini. Le ministre algérien est accompagné dans ce déplacement par le PDG du groupe Sonatrach, entouré des responsables des principales filiales du géant algérien des hydrocarbures. Cette mission s’inscrit dans le cadre du suivi et de l’évaluation de l’état d’avancement des projets et accords de coopération bilatérale entre l’Algérie et le Niger dans le domaine des hydrocarbures. Elle porte notamment sur le projet de recherche et d’exploration pétrolière dans le bloc de Kafra, conduit par Sonatrach (via sa filiale SIPEX) en partenariat avec la Société nigérienne des produits pétroliers (Sonidep). Elle s’inscrit dans une dynamique élargie de coopération énergétique entre l’Algérie et le Niger. Cette collaboration inclut les perspectives de développement de nouveaux blocs, notamment le bloc de Bilma, identifié comme axe complémentaire stratégique. Elle s’accompagne également d’un suivi attentif de l’état d’avancement du projet de gazoduc transsaharien (TSGP), infrastructure majeure reliant l’Algérie, le Niger et le Nigeria, et appelée à renforcer l’intégration énergétique régionale. Le gazoduc transsaharien constitue l’un des principaux dossiers de cette visite. D’une longueur totale de 4 128 km, il doit relier Warri, dans le sud du Nigeria, à Hassi R’mel en Algérie, en traversant le Niger sur 841 km. L’Algérie a lancé, en juin 2026, les travaux de réalisation du tronçon algérien du projet, tandis que les préparatifs et les études relatifs au tronçon situé sur le territoire nigérien se poursuivent. Le TSGP est considéré comme un projet stratégique visant à renforcer l’intégration énergétique régionale et à développer les infrastructures gazières en Afrique. Sur le bloc de Kafra, une nouvelle phase d’exploration a été lancée le 13 août 2026, avec une campagne de quatre puits d’exploration étalés sur deux ans, confiés à l’Entreprise nationale de forage (ENAFOR), filiale de Sonatrach. Les autorités nigériennes ont prolongé de deux ans, le 15 avril 2026, l’autorisation d’exploration de SIPEX, afin de permettre la délimitation et l’évaluation du gisement. Selon les estimations prospectives citées par le ministère nigérien du Pétrole, le 9 septembre dernier, le bloc de Kafra recèlerait jusqu’à 2,5 milliards de barils de ressources prospectives, avec environ 255 millions de barils de réserves 2P (prouvées et probables) associés à une découverte évaluée en 2018. Durant son séjour à Niamey, le ministre d’État algérien sera reçu en audience par les plus hautes autorités du Niger. Ces rencontres devraient permettre de passer en revue l’ensemble du partenariat dans les hydrocarbures, y compris les questions de raffinage et de pétrochimie, ainsi que le suivi des grands travaux de maintenance de la raffinerie de Zinder. Cette visite intervient dans un contexte de dynamisation des relations algéro-nigériennes, marquée par une volonté commune de concrétiser rapidement les projets énergétiques structurants pour les deux pays et pour la région sahélienne. items.title: FG has no immediate plan to hike electricity tariff – Tegbe
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has no immediate plan to increase electricity tariffs, Minister of Power, Mr. Joseph Tegbe, said on Monday, dismissing rumours of an impending hike in electricity rates across the country. Tegbe, who spoke in Abuja while presenting his scorecard for his first 100 days in office, said electricity generation and transmission had exceeded 5,000 megawatts (MW) in recent weeks, compared with between 3,700MW and 4,700MW before June 2026. He disclosed that the sector recorded a generation peak of 5,330MW in August and September, following interventions to restore power infrastructure and improve the performance of existing assets. The Minister, however, acknowledged that the improvements had yet to translate into reliable electricity supply for many Nigerians, saying the immediate task was to sustain the gains and extend them to more communities. Speaking on his performance between June 8 and September 16, 2026, Tegbe said the administration had focused on stabilising the electricity value chain, restoring market discipline and strengthening governance. He said: “Operational record reports show generation and transmission above 5,000MW over the past couple of weeks, compared to the 3,700 to 4,700MW range before June, and a generation peak of 5,330MW during August and September. “Our next task is to sustain these gains and translate them into more dependable supply at customer level.” The Minister said the 375MW Alaoji open-cycle power plant, which had been offline for three years, was restored to the national grid during the period. He also disclosed that the commissioning of new transformers at Apapa, Ijora, Alausa and Lekki in Lagos had unlocked 672MW of transmission capacity. Similarly, a new 300-megavolt-ampere (MVA) transformer energised at Katampe, Abuja, unlocked an additional 240MW of transmission capacity. According to him, the interventions were aimed at recovering stranded capacity and strengthening electricity delivery to major centres of demand. Tegbe said the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had also secured the release of more than 300 containers of critical power equipment held up at the ports. He said the equipment would be inspected, deployed and installed to support ongoing transmission infrastructure upgrades. On electricity access, the minister said 62 solar and mini-grid installations had been completed across 30 states, providing about 43.6MW of installed solar capacity and 41,735 new connections. The projects, he said, had an estimated beneficiary reach of more than 208,000 people. He listed initiatives under the Rural Electrification Agency, including the 3MW solar hybrid system recently commissioned at Yakubu Gowon University, Abuja, as part of efforts to provide more dependable electricity to educational institutions. Other projects include a 20MW off-grid initiative in Kogi State, a 3.5MW solar project in Kebbi State, a 5.5MW mini-grid in Epe, Lagos, and 39 mini-grids in Adamawa State designed to provide nearly 27MW of electricity. The Minister said the Renewable Asset Management Company (RAMCO) would manage publicly financed renewable energy infrastructure and mobilise N3 trillion over the coming years. On the financial health of the sector, Tegbe said the government had raised an estimated N1.23 trillion towards settling outstanding power-sector debts as part of a broader programme to address N3.3 trillion in liabilities. He said the initiative was expected to improve liquidity across the electricity value chain and strengthen operators’ capacity to maintain infrastructure and meet their obligations. The Minister also disclosed that the government had blocked revenue leakages associated with energy theft and other losses along the Ikorodu-Sagamu industrial corridor, estimated at approximately N120 billion annually. He said improved billing, collection and remittance would help preserve resources needed to sustain electricity supply. On metering, Tegbe said approximately 350,000 meters were installed during his first 100 days in office, bringing cumulative installations to 1,004,260 as of August 2026. He added that the resolution of the AMMON litigation had unlocked the procurement of about 1.4 million smart meters across affected programmes. The Minister said metering of military formations was also progressing, with 90,000 installations recorded, while 5,000 young Nigerians were undergoing training as smart-meter installers under the Power Force programme. Tegbe reiterated that the government had no immediate plan to increase electricity tariffs. He said the next phase of the reform programme would focus on stabilising key transmission corridors, including Lagos, Enugu-Port Harcourt and Abuja-Kaduna-Kano, while advancing the proposed Transmission Super Grid. The Minister said technical audits had commenced along the Lagos and Abuja corridors to identify weak points and guide investments towards interventions with measurable system impact. He added that the government would also pursue bilateral arrangements between generation and distribution companies to improve capacity utilisation and payment certainty. On future investments, Tegbe said engagements with Chinese companies had secured commitments to accelerate priority power projects, including the 1.9-gigawatt Presidential Power Initiative, with the first transmission lines scheduled for delivery in the first quarter of 2027. He said the government would continue efforts to strengthen grid protection and control systems, improve gas availability to power plants, and address vandalism and electricity theft. Acknowledging that the national generation peak did not necessarily reflect the electricity experience of every community, Tegbe said the government would measure progress through supply reliability, billing accuracy, and the resolution of faults and complaints. He said the government would work over the next six months to translate the repairs and reforms into more visible improvements in electricity supply. The post FG has no immediate plan to hike electricity tariff – Tegbe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Tinubu’s vacation: Who is in charge of Nigeria? Atiku asks
items.description: Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has questioned who is constitutionally exercising presidential authority in Nigeria following the expiration of the three-week vacation announced for President Bola Tinubu. Tinubu left Nigeria on August 30 for what the Presidency described as a three-week working vacation in Europe. The Presidency said on Monday that the President had extended his stay by a few days and would return to Nigeria at the weekend. In a statement titled “Who is in Charge of Nigeria?”, Atiku cited Section 145 of the 1999 Constitution, which provides for the President to transmit a written declaration to the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House when proceeding on vacation, allowing the Vice President to perform presidential functions as Acting President. He said Nigerians had not been shown any such communication transferring presidential authority to Vice President Kashim Shettima. “Twenty-one days have come and gone since President Bola Ahmed Tinubu left Nigeria on what the Presidency described as a three-week annual vacation,” Atiku said. “Today, Nigerians are entitled to ask a very simple constitutional question: Who is in charge of Nigeria?” According to Atiku, if the required declaration was not transmitted within 21 days, Section 145(2) provides for the National Assembly to mandate the Vice President to perform the functions of President as Acting President. He therefore challenged the Presidency to publish the letter if it exists and asked the National Assembly to explain why the constitutional procedure had not been activated if no declaration was transmitted. “If such a letter exists, the Presidency should publish it immediately,” he said. The ADC candidate also raised concerns over the simultaneous absence of Tinubu and Shettima, with the Vice President in New York representing Nigeria at the 81st United Nations General Assembly. “So again: who is exercising presidential authority in Nigeria today, and under what constitutional instrument?” Atiku asked. He described the matter as one of “constitutional order” rather than political convenience, adding that Nigeria could not be governed through informal arrangements. “Nigeria cannot be governed by assumptions. It cannot be governed by presidential social-media posts from Europe. “It cannot be governed by photographs from private dinners at the Élysée Palace. “It cannot be governed on autopilot,” he said. Atiku also cited the deaths of 37 Nigerians in NSCDC custody in Minna and rising petrol prices, which he said had added to the economic difficulties facing Nigerians. “These are not ordinary times. Yet the President is abroad. The Vice President is abroad. The Senate President is abroad,” he said. He called on the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House to confirm whether they received any communication from Tinubu under Section 145(1). Atiku added: “Nigeria is bigger than any President. At a time of severe economic hardship, rising energy costs, security challenges and the shocking deaths of citizens in government custody, the country deserves visible, accountable and constitutionally grounded leadership.” “The question will not disappear: Who, constitutionally, is in charge of Nigeria?” The post Tinubu’s vacation: Who is in charge of Nigeria? Atiku asks appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Abiodun moves to reconcile aggrieved APC members in Ogun East
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has moved to reconcile aggrieved members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) who lost in the party’s recent primaries, assuring them that there would be room for all within the party. Abiodun, who spoke on Monday in Ijebu-Ode during a meeting with APC leaders and stakeholders in Ijebu-Ode Local Government Area, directed the immediate establishment of a reconciliation committee to reach out to aggrieved members, address their concerns and give them a sense of belonging. The governor said the reconciliation effort was critical to strengthening the party ahead of the 2027 general elections, stressing that those who contested and lost the primaries remained important members of the APC. “I want us to set up a reconciliation committee in Ijebu-Ode because I know that we have some of our members who are still angry. I want us to be aggressive about that reconciliation. Let us appeal to them. I am ready to implement the report of the reconciliation you will submit to me,” he said. Abiodun directed that the committee be headed by Chief Olu Okuboyejo, with former Deputy Governor, Yetunde Onanuga and State Commissioner serving as members. He also directed that similar reconciliation committees be established at the ward and local government levels to ensure that no aggrieved member was left out of the process. The governor assured party members that the objective was not only to reconcile those who lost in the primaries, but also to accommodate everyone who remained committed to the party. “We must reach out to them, give them a sense of belonging, assuage their concerns and ensure proper reconciliation. There is room for everybody,” he said. Abiodun said elections were about numbers, urging party leaders to bring back members who might have become aggrieved while simultaneously expanding the APC’s membership base by welcoming new members from opposition parties. “Those who were not with us before were the ones disturbing us and making sure our votes in Ijebu-Ode are not 100 per cent. But now that they are with us, our victory is certainly 100 per cent sure. Let us welcome them,” he said. The governor urged party members to concentrate on issue-based campaigns, saying the APC had a record of performance at both the state and federal levels. He said his administration had grown Ogun State’s economy to about N17 trillion, while internally generated revenue had risen to N250 billion and was projected to reach N300 billion before the end of the year. Abiodun described the meeting as the formal commencement of his political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections and appreciated the people of Ijebu-Ode for their support for the APC in the 2019 and 2023 elections. He assured the people that his administration would continue to improve infrastructure and deliver more dividends of democracy to the area. The Director-General of the Campaign Committee, Senator Lekan Mustapha, said Ijebu-Ode, being the headquarters of Ogun East Senatorial District, had a significant voter population that must be effectively mobilised for the party ahead of the elections. He noted that the local government had 161 polling units, stressing the need for effective mobilisation across all the units. The governor later held similar meetings with APC leaders and executives in Ijebu-North East and Odogbolu Local Government Areas as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structure ahead of the 2027 elections. The post Abiodun moves to reconcile aggrieved APC members in Ogun East appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Audience du Président du Faso : « Jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les lauréates du concours « HAKILI Mousso »
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a reçu ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 en audience, les lauréates du concours de détection de talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso », conduite par la Ministre Conseillère spéciale du Président du Faso, chargée du Développement technologique, la Camarade Dr Floriane OUÉDRAOGO/ZONGO. Ce lundi 21 septembre était « jour de rentrée » à Koulouba pour les filles lauréates du concours national de détection des talents scientifiques féminins « HAKILI Mousso » et les meilleurs enseignants dans les disciplines scientifiques. Dans cette “salle de classe” d’une heure, ils ont eu droit à une master class du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, sur l’importance des disciplines scientifiques dans le développement. Outre les félicitations pour leur esprit d’abnégation, de surpassement de soi, le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire a prodigué des conseils aux lauréates. Il s’agit entre autres de l’amour des métiers scientifiques, du travail, de la confiance en soi. « Ne vous fixez-pas de limites. Vous êtes capables de tout faire. (…) Demain, nous attendons de vous des ingénieurs en mécanique, mécatronique, électronique, en physique, en astrologie. Vous devez vous donner des objectifs et les atteindre », a dit le Chef de l’État. HAKILI Mousso, un creuset pour l’éclosion d’une élite féminine Le Leader de la Révolution Progressiste Populaire, a rappelé que le Concours « HAKILI Mousso » ne s’inscrit pas dans la politique du genre importée par les impérialistes avec le dessein d’opposer les femmes aux hommes. « Nous nous inscrivons dans une politique d’élite. Encourager les femmes vers certains métiers qui nous intéressent », a indiqué le Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Au cours de cette audience, le Président du Faso a réitéré son engagement pour le développement du Burkina Faso dont la clé de voûte repose sur la qualité des ressources humaines. La première en chimie à « HAKILI Mousso », Inès Marie Fabiolas NIKIEMA est ressortie bien confiante de l’entretien avec le Chef de l’État. Celle qui rêve de faire carrière dans l’aéronautique pour participer à développer son pays, a pris l’engagement de bien travailler et afin d’être un modèle pour les autres jeunes. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: Louga : 16 cas de diphtérie recensés, dont un décès
items.description: La région de Louga a enregistré 16 cas de diphtérie, dont un décès, a indiqué lundi 21 septembre la gouverneure Ndèye Nguénar Mbodji. Les autorités sanitaires régionales annoncent le renforcement des mesures de vaccination, de surveillance et de sensibilisation pour contenir la maladie. La situation épidémiologique liée à la diphtérie a été au centre d’un comité régional de gestion des épidémies tenu lundi à Louga, d'après l'APS. À cette occasion, la Gouverneure Ndèye Nguénar Mbodji a fait état de 16 cas recensés dans la région, dont un mortel. Selon elle, plusieurs mesures de prévention et de riposte sont en cours pour limiter la propagation de la maladie. Le dispositif repose notamment sur la vaccination, la sensibilisation et la communication auprès des populations. Des rencontres sont prévues dans les trois départements de la région ainsi qu’au niveau local, sous la coordination des sous-préfets, avec l’implication des différents acteurs territoriaux. Les autorités sanitaires comptent également intensifier les campagnes de vaccination afin de rapprocher les équipes de santé des populations et d’améliorer la couverture vaccinale. La gouverneure a, par ailleurs, appelé les prestataires de santé à davantage partager les informations sanitaires disponibles. Elle a estimé que ces données constituent des outils essentiels à la prise de décision et à l’orientation des politiques publiques. Un plaidoyer sera ainsi porté auprès des autorités compétentes pour contribuer à lever les éventuels obstacles à la transmission de ces informations. Le directeur régional de la Santé de Louga, Dr Moustapha Faye, a insisté sur la nécessité de reconnaître rapidement les signes de la diphtérie. Il a notamment cité les difficultés à avaler, les douleurs à la gorge, la fièvre et l’apparition de taches blanchâtres au niveau de la gorge. La détresse respiratoire, la rhinorrhée et les saignements de nez peuvent également constituer des signes d’alerte, a-t-il précisé. En cas de symptômes suspects, il recommande de se rendre sans délai dans la structure de santé la plus proche afin de permettre la consultation, la confirmation du diagnostic et la prise en charge. Le Dr Faye a également rappelé l’importance de la vaccination dans la prévention de la maladie. Il a indiqué que les enfants de 0 à 5 ans doivent bénéficier d’une vaccination complète administrée en trois doses, respectivement à la sixième, à la dixième et à la quatorzième semaine. Les autorités sanitaires recommandent par ailleurs le respect des mesures barrières, notamment le port du masque pour les personnes malades ou suspectes et la limitation des contacts rapprochés. Les personnes ayant été en contact étroit avec un cas doivent également faire l’objet d’un suivi par les équipes sanitaires. La diphtérie se transmet notamment par les gouttelettes respiratoires émises lors de la parole, de la toux ou des éternuements.

items.title: Alleged Rights Violation: AGF asks court to dismiss El-Rufai’s N1bn suit
items.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA—The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, has asked the Federal High Court in Abuja to dismiss, as lacking in merit, the N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit that the former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai, filed against him and the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). The Inspector-General of Police was also listed as a respondent in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026. El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, dragged the respondents to court over an alleged unlawful raid on his Abuja residence. He specifically challenged the legality of the warrant the ICPC relied on to search his home. He prayed the court to declare that the search warrant dated February 4, which the Chief Magistrate of the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT signed to authorise the search and seizure of items from his residence, was invalid, null, and void. The former governor also sought a declaration that the search warrant was legally defective for lacking particularity, and for “material drafting errors, ambiguity in execution parameters, overbreadth, and absence of probable cause, thereby constituting an unlawful and unreasonable search in violation of Section 37 of the Constitution.” Other reliefs he sought include a declaration that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on February 19 at about 2 p.m., executed by agents of the ICPC and the Inspector-General of Police under the invalid warrant, “amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights to dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” The Chief Magistrate, who was initially listed as the 2nd respondent, was subsequently delisted from the case by the applicant. At the resumed proceedings on Monday, the AGF, through a lawyer from the Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Maimuna Lami-Shiru, notified the court of a counter-affidavit he had filed to challenge the competence of the suit. The AGF, among other things, contended that the former governor failed to disclose any reasonable cause of action to warrant the grant of the reliefs he is seeking from the court. While denying the allegation that the applicant’s rights were violated, the AGF insisted that both the ICPC and the IGP acted within the bounds of the law. He, therefore, urged the court to dismiss the suit. Meanwhile, Justice Joyce Abdulmalik adjourned the case until October 27 to allow El-Rufai’s lawyer, Akinyemi Aremu, to respond to the AGF’s counter-affidavit. The ICPC had earlier urged the court to dismiss the suit, insisting it acted on the strength of a petition that was filed against the former governor. The agency told the court that El-Rufai’s house was searched as part of its investigations into the petition, adding that its operatives acted with a valid search warrant issued on February 18. The commission said its officials were accompanied by police officers and that the search was conducted in the presence of the applicant’s wife, Hadiza El-Rufai, and his son, Mohammed El-Rufai. Likewise, the police, in their own counter-affidavit deposed to by Inspector Ewa Anthony, maintained that they had the statutory power to detect, arrest, investigate and prosecute offenders. The police told the court that their officers lawfully executed a search warrant that was issued by a competent court. El-Rufai currently faces multiple charges, including an allegation that he unlawfully intercepted the phone communications of the National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu. The ICPC had obtained court permission on March 12 to examine and analyse about 14 sets of electronic devices allegedly recovered when the former governor’s house was searched. It disclosed that the recovered items included a Sony HD-EGS storage device; a 1TB Transcend storage device; a Toshiba storage device; a Samsung mobile phone; a Nokia mobile phone (96GB); a BlackBerry mobile phone; a Google IDEOS phone; a Samsung storage device (SPO802N); a reMarkable tablet; an Apple MacBook Pro (black); a Seagate FreeAgent desk external drive; a ZTE mobile phone; 10 flash drives; and a MicroSD memory card. In his suit, El-Rufai prayed the court, among other things, to declare that any evidence obtained pursuant to the invalid warrant and unlawful search “is inadmissible in any proceedings against the applicant, as it was procured in breach of constitutional safeguards.” He further applied for an injunction restraining the respondents and their agents from further relying on, using, or tendering any evidence or items seized during the unlawful search in any investigation, prosecution, or proceedings involving him. El-Rufai also asked the court to direct the first and third respondents (ICPC and Inspector-General of Police) to return forthwith all items seized from his Abuja home during the unlawful search, together with a detailed inventory. Likewise, he sought “an order awarding the sum of N1,000,000,000.00 (One Billion Naira) as general, exemplary, and aggravated damages against the respondents, jointly and severally, for the violations of the applicant’s fundamental rights, including trespass, unlawful seizure, and the resultant psychological trauma, humiliation, distress, infringement of privacy, and reputational harm.” From the total sum sought, the applicant explained that N300m would serve as compensatory damages for psychological trauma, emotional distress, and loss of personal security; N400m as exemplary damages to deter future misconduct by law enforcement agencies and vindicate the applicant’s rights; and N300m as aggravated damages for “the malicious, high-handed, and oppressive nature of the respondents’ actions, including the use of a patently defective warrant procured through misleading representations.” He prayed to be awarded N100m to cover the cost of the litigation. items.title: Oudalan/Salubrité: l’AJD et l’association Laabi Jam nettoient l’orphelinat Baadé Soukabé à Gorom-Gorom
items.description: BURKINA-OUDALAN-SALUBRITE-ORPHELINAT Oudalan/Salubrité: l’AJD et l’association Laabi Jam nettoient l'orphelinat Baadé Soukabé à Gorom-Gorom Gorom-Gorom, 19 sept. 2026 (AIB)- L’Association jeunesse et développement (AJD), en collaboration avec l’association Laabi Jam, a organisé, samedi à Gorom-Gorom, une journée de salubrité et de désherbage au profit de l’orphelinat Baadé Soukabé. L’initiative a mobilisé des autorités locales, des acteurs de la société civile ainsi que des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS). Munis de balais, de râteaux, de pelles et de brouettes, les participants ont nettoyé des différents espaces de l’orphelinat, notamment les cours, les dortoirs et les alentours immédiats du centre. L’opération a permis de débarrasser les lieux des herbes hautes, des ordures ménagères et des déchets plastiques, contribuant ainsi à améliorer le cadre de vie des pensionnaires. Selon le président de l’AJD, Amadou Guibrilla Maïga, cette initiative s’inscrit dans la volonté des associations de promouvoir la citoyenneté active et la solidarité au sein des communautés. Il a salué la mobilisation des FDS et de l’ensemble des participants qui, selon lui, ont consacré leur temps et leur énergie à rendre le centre plus propre et plus accueillant pour les enfants. « Maintenir un cadre de vie propre au sein d’un établissement pour enfants relève d’un devoir à la fois patriotique, citoyen et profondément humain », a-t-il souligné. Cette journée de salubrité a également constitué un cadre de mobilisation citoyenne et de solidarité autour de l’orphelinat Baadé Soukabé. À travers ce type d’initiative, les organisateurs entendent encourager davantage l’engagement communautaire en faveur d’un environnement sain et du bien-être des enfants. items.title: FG threatens to shut Lagos-Calabar highway shutdown over violations
items.description: …Gives motorists two weeks to comply with rules LAGOS — The Federal Government has given motorists and other road users on the Lagos section of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway two weeks to comply with safety regulations or face a shutdown of the route. The Federal Controller of Works in Lagos State, Olufemi Dare, issued the ultimatum on Monday during an inspection of the highway, citing dangerous speeding, vandalism, illegal parking and other activities threatening safety along the route. Dare said the directive followed concerns raised by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, over persistent breaches of safety measures on the highway. “Within two weeks, if there’s no improvement on all these issues, then we have no option than to come back and shut down this road,” he said. The controller said the government had the Lekki-Epe Expressway as an alternative route, stressing that the coastal highway remained under construction and should ordinarily not have been opened to traffic before the completion of its bridges. The Lagos section of the highway spans about 103 kilometres and consists of two sections — Section 1, covering approximately 47km, and Section 2, about 56km. According to Dare, the two sections have 20 major bridges, 10 in each section, with several still under construction. He expressed concern over motorists exceeding the prescribed 30km/h speed limit, particularly on sections where construction work is ongoing. “People who come to coastal road and get to a speed of 120 kilometres per hour on the coastal road, and where constructions are going on, bridges, construction are going on,” Dare said. “We have said your speed on the coastal road must not be more than 30 kilometres per hour.” Dare said the government was concerned about reports of deaths on the highway, warning that it could no longer allow unsafe practices to continue. He also warned articulated vehicle operators against parking trucks and trailers along the highway, saying the practice posed additional risks to motorists. On security, Dare disclosed that the government had reached an agreement with the Lagos State Police Command to increase police deployment along the route. He said the decision followed meetings between Umahi and the state Commissioner of Police, Fatai Tijani. “Beginning from this morning, we’ve started to see the improvement in deployment of police. And we are going to have more,” he said. The controller also warned against illegal U-turns along the highway, saying anyone arrested for creating or using such points would be prosecuted. He said commercial motorcycles, tricycles, hawking and animal grazing had also been prohibited along the route. “We don’t want Okada motorcycles, tricycles. We don’t want them on the coastal road,” Dare said. He added that authorities would also remove shanties and other illegal structures along the highway. Dare identified vandalism of safety infrastructure as another major challenge, disclosing that about five kilometres of ClearVu fencing had been removed, while approximately 18 kilometres of concrete covers had been vandalised and taken away. “They come in the night, they remove the ClearVu fence that was used to barricade the communities from the coastal highway,” he said. He said the government was considering replacing the steel ClearVu fencing with concrete barriers in vulnerable areas because the existing fencing could be easily removed. “We have to change the strategy. In areas where we have block work today, we do not have any problem with them,” he said. Dare further disclosed that plans were underway to deploy CCTV cameras to improve surveillance along the highway. He said the government had approved the recruitment of 40 coastal guards for Section 1, with four to be drawn from each community along the route. The guards, he explained, would work with the police to provide community-level surveillance, while additional personnel would be recruited for Section 2. Dare said some previously engaged coastal guards had been attacked by vandals, underscoring the need for stronger police protection. He added that the government planned to reorganise and train the coastal guards under the direct supervision of the Lagos State Police Command. items.title: Dangote Refinery IPO reflects long-term commitment to Africa’s industrial transformation – Dangote
items.description: By Udeme Akpan President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has said the ongoing Dangote Petroleum Refinery Initial Public Offering, IPO, reflects the Group’s long-term commitment to Africa’s industrialisation, wealth creation and economic development. Speaking during an interview with Bloomberg Television, Dangote said the IPO was designed not only to raise capital but also to broaden African ownership of a major strategic asset. “For decades, Africa’s most strategic assets have been owned by a limited group of investors. Through this IPO, we are creating an opportunity for millions of Africans to become part-owners of a transformative business that is changing the energy landscape of the continent,” he said. According to him, the offering would give ordinary Africans and institutional investors an opportunity to participate in the growth of the refinery and share in the value created by the project. “It is about creating value, expanding prosperity, and building generational wealth for our people,” Dangote said. He described the refinery as an African response to the continent’s longstanding energy challenges, noting that the project was conceived to reduce dependence on imported petroleum products while strengthening local production. “Our objective has always been bigger than building a refinery. We want to create institutions that will outlive us, businesses that can compete globally, and opportunities that allow Africans to share in the wealth created on the continent,” he stated. Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s capacity would be expanded from its current 700,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day over the coming years. He said the expansion would strengthen the refinery’s position among the world’s largest refining complexes and increase Africa’s capacity to meet its energy requirements. Dangote added that proceeds from the IPO would support the expansion programme, while the company also plans to seek a listing on the New York Stock Exchange after completing the next phase of development. According to him, the proposed international listing would provide access to global capital and further expose African industrial assets to international investors. On investor confidence, Dangote said strong demand during the refinery’s private placement demonstrated significant interest in the project. He explained that the amount raised through the private placement was deliberately limited to allow for wider participation in the subsequent public offering. The industrialist said the Group’s broader investment strategy would continue to focus on sectors capable of driving industrial growth, including refining, petrochemicals, cement, fertiliser and manufacturing. “Africa has the resources, the talent and the market. What we need is to continue to industrialise and create businesses that can compete globally,” he said. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery IPO has attracted significant attention from investors and market participants, coming as the company seeks to broaden ownership of the refinery while raising funds for further expansion. items.title: Naqvi meets Iranian counterpart, president; Tehran lauds Pakistan's efforts for regional peace
items.description: Tehran on Monday thanked Pakistan’s military and civilian leadership for its efforts for regional peace and stability as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met with his Iranian counterpart Eskandar Momeni in Tehran. Later, he also held a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, according to Iran’s state-run Press TV . According to Pakistan’s interior ministry, Naqvi and Momeni exchanged views on “Pakistan-Iran bilateral relations and the latest situation in the region”. The statement said the Iranian minister thanked Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for their efforts towards advancing peace in the region. “We are grateful for Pakistan’s continuous efforts to establish peace in the region,” Momeni was cited as saying, adding that the visit from the Pakistani side was “beneficial”. The ministers also reviewed progress on the ongoing cooperation between their interior ministries in various sectors, the statement added. Naqvi, meanwhile, said that “bilateral relations will become even stronger” between Pakistan and Iran in the coming days. Earlier, Iranian media outlets reported that Naqvi had arrived in Tehran and was received at the airport by Momeni. Naqvi’s visit to Tehran comes as Pakistan continues its diplomatic efforts to rescue the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed in July between the United States and Iran and intended to end the conflict that began with US-Israeli attacks on Iran in late February. Although Pakistan has been pivotal in facilitating talks and the interim ceasefire over the course of the conflict, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB cited the country’s foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei as saying on Saturday that Naqvi’s visit would “focus on bilateral relations, and there is no plan to exchange any specific messages regarding mediation”. In July, Naqvi met with Momeni as the latter undertook an official visit to Pakistan, where the two reviewed bilateral relations, trade, regional developments and avenues for cooperation.

items.description: Algérie Ferries chamboule à nouveau le programme de ses traversées entre les ports algériens et français. Après le report des horaires de départ de Marseille – Bejaïa et Bejaïa – Marseille, c’est au tour de deux autres dessertes de connaître le même sort. La Société nationale de transport maritime de passagers (ENTMV) a informé ce lundi via un communiqué qu'une « modification indépendante de sa volonté » a affecté les horaires des traversées Marseille – Alger et Alger – Marseille. Pour la première, qui était prévue le mercredi 23 septembre, elle est reportée au samedi 26 septembre à 12h00. Pour la seconde, le ferry qui devait initialement quitter le port d’Alger jeudi 24 septembre 2026 va finalement partir lundi 28 septembre à 12h00. Algérie Ferries : cinq modifications depuis début septembre Algérie Ferries présente ses excuses pour la gêne occasionnée aux passagers qui ont réservé sur deux dessertes maritimes, mais comme d’habitude, la compagnie maritime de transport de voyageurs ne donne pas les raisons des fréquents reports de ses traversées. Depuis le début du mois de septembre, l'ENTMV a chamboulé à 5 reprises le programme de ses traversées. Le 3 septembre, elle a annoncé le report de la desserte Annaba – Marseille. Quatre jours après, le 7 septembre, c’est la desserte Alger – Marseille qui a subi le même sort. Le 9 septembre, les horaires de départ des ferries Marseille – Bejaïa et Bejaïa – Marseille ont été changés. Le 13 septembre, la modification a touché la desserte Marseille – Oran. Des reports qui impactent les passagers dont certains se déplacent de loin pour prendre le bateau. D’autant que l’ENTMV est pratiquement le seul transporteur maritime qui chamboule régulièrement le programme de ses traversées. L’article Algérie Ferries reporte les traversées Marseille – Alger et Alger – Marseille est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: 2027: Ogun West exclusion drives Adeola’s ambition, says Aide
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship campaign of Senator Solomon Adeola has anchored his 2027 ambition on what it described as the long-standing exclusion of Ogun West Senatorial District from producing a governor of Ogun State. Media Adviser and Chief of Staff to Adeola, Kayode Odunaro, said Ogun West had been unable to produce a governor of the state for about five decades, describing the situation as one of the factors driving the senator’s ambition. Odunaro, who is also Chairman of the Media and Publicity Committee of the Ogun State APC Campaign Council, stated this on Monday during an interview on a current affairs programme on Eagle 102.5 FM, Ilese-Ijebu, Ogun State. He said Adeola’s ambition was not merely about securing political power for Ogun West but was also aimed at addressing what he described as an imbalance in political representation and development across the state. “Senator Solomon Adeola happens to come from a district in Ogun West where, over the past 50 years and counting, they have not been opportuned to govern Ogun State as a whole,” Odunaro said. He linked the issue of political representation to development challenges in the district, particularly the Yewa-Awori axis. According to him, residents of the area have continued to express concerns over the level of infrastructure and development in Ogun West compared with other parts of the state. “The people of Yewa have been complaining; looking at all the infrastructure in Ogun West, it happens to be like third class in Ogun State,” he said. Odunaro said Adeola’s governorship bid was therefore being presented as an opportunity to address the perceived imbalance and improve development across Ogun West and the state generally. “Solomon Adeola is coming to Ogun State to fight and regain Ogun State reputation and legacy. Yewa-Awori have been excluded completely from being in government,” he said. The campaign official also cited Adeola’s record as a senator, arguing that his interventions had attracted development projects beyond his immediate constituency. He said the senator had contributed to infrastructure development across Ogun State, particularly through road projects and other interventions. “Senator Solomon Adeola has done things that are unprecedented. Solomon Adeola has done more in infrastructure in Ogun State; about 300 road infrastructure have been done and some are being repaired by him,” Odunaro said. He added that the interventions were intended to reduce what he described as the development gap between Ogun West and other parts of the state. “Senator Adeola has done enough to bring the infrastructure to a level that is comparable to, if not better than, the one in Ogun Central or Ogun East,” he said. Odunaro maintained that Adeola’s ambition should be viewed within the broader context of governing Ogun State rather than as an exclusively Ogun West project. He said an Adeola administration would build on the achievements of the incumbent governor, Dapo Abiodun. “The governor of our state has done very well, whatever Senator Solomon Adeola is doing will complement it,” he said. Odunaro also described the proposed transition as different from what he characterised as a history of difficult political succession in the state. “Definitely, he is going to embark on continuity of the current governor’s agenda, Dapo Abiodun… Over time, Ogun State has had hostile succession. This will be the first time there will be a harmonious succession,” he said. On the possibility of constructing a new airport in Ogun West, Odunaro said the project was not among Adeola’s immediate priorities, arguing that the state already had an existing airport. “Building a new airport in Yewa is not a critical agenda for Senator Solomon Adeola, whereas we have one over there that is working perfectly,” he said. According to him, the focus would instead be on upgrading the existing facility and making it commercially viable for the benefit of the state. “He is just going to improve on the already existing one. Maybe take it to a level that it will be so commercially viable that Ogun will continue to benefit from it,” Odunaro said. Odunaro said the 2027 governorship election should ultimately be about the capacity of candidates to deliver development and represent the interests of residents across Ogun State. items.title: CAN U17 : accueil chaleureux à Conakry pour le Syli Cadet, qualifié pour la phase finale au Maroc
items.description: Le Syli Cadet a regagné Conakry ce lundi 21 septembre 2026, au lendemain de sa qualification pour la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN) U17 au Maroc. La sélection guinéenne a été accueillie à l’aéroport international Ahmed Sékou Touré par des supporters et plusieurs responsables sportifs. La Guinée a décroché son billet pour la phase finale en s’imposant (2-0) face au Liberia, samedi 20 septembre, lors du match pour la troisième place du tournoi qualificatif de la zone UFOA-A, disputé au stade Léopold Sédar Senghor de Dakar. Cette qualification permet au Syli Cadet de retrouver la CAN U17 après 8 années d’absence. Pour le sélectionneur Sékouba Camara, cette qualification vient concrétiser un travail rigoureux mené avec un groupe déterminé : « C'est un bilan très satisfaisant. L'objectif principal, c'était la qualification. La Guinée en avait besoin, cela faisait sept ans qu'on galérait derrière ça. Je dis félicitations à mes gamins et au staff. Désormais, l'objectif principal pour la phase finale est de se qualifier pour la Coupe du Monde. » Capitaine et joueur clé de cette effectif, Fodé Moussa Traoré a tenu à associer tout le peuple guinéen à ce succès collectif : « C'est une qualification très importante pour nous. On tient à remercier le peuple guinéen pour tout le soutien qu'il nous a apporté depuis le début. On est fiers d'avoir validé cette qualification avec tout le staff et tous nos coéquipiers. » Screenshot Côté dirigeants, cette performance s'inscrit dans une volonté globale de restructuration du football de base en Guinée. Le Secrétaire général adjoint de la fédération guinéenne de football a souligné la portée stratégique de ce résultat : « Nous accueillons l'équipe avec ferveur et chaleur pour lui dire merci pour cet honneur et cette fierté. En tant que managers du football, nous continuerons à créer l'environnement le plus épanouissant possible pour ces jeunes, afin d'alimenter les catégories supérieures en talents purs. » s'est rejouit Mamady Kaba. Screenshot De son côté, Aboubacar Diakité, chef de la délégation guinéenne à Dakar, a salué l'union sacrée qui a régné autour du groupe tout au long de la compétition : « Depuis qu'on est partis, on s'est donné la main avec un seul objectif : qualifier l'équipe pour la CAN U17. Je tiens à remercier les joueurs, le staff technique, le ministre des Sports et le chef de l'État, le Mamadi Doumbouya, pour tout le soutien apporté au sport guinéen . » Screenshot Désormais qualifié pour le rendez-vous continental au Maroc, le Syli Cadet va pouvoir se projeter vers la préparation de la compétition avec une ambition affirmée : décrocher l'un des tickets qualificatifs pour le mondial de la catégorie.

items.title: Ahafo Ano South West DCE laid to rest as Muslims hold final prayers
items.description: A deep sense of sorrow has engulfed Mankranso in the Ahafo Ano South West District of the Ashanti Region following the sudden death of the District Chief Executive, Abubakar Sedik. The late DCE was laid to rest today, Monday, September 21, following his passing on September 20 after a short illness. As part of Islamic burial traditions, the Muslim community in Mankranso gathered at the Mankranso School Park to offer final Salat al-Janazah prayers for the deceased and bid him a solemn farewell. Scores of mourners, residents, sympathisers, friends and members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) gathered in grief to pay their last respects to the late DCE. The atmosphere was filled with sorrow and tears as mourners struggled to come to terms with the sudden loss of a man who served as the District Chief Executive of the area. The news of Abubakar Sedik’s death has left the people of Mankranso and the wider Ahafo Ano South West District in deep mourning. According to the local assembly, the DCE died on Sunday evening, 20th September, after stakeholders met with the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, in Kumasi. The Minister was in Kumasi to engage stakeholders on the completion of the Kejetia Phase Two Redevelopment project. Mr Sedik reportedly fell ill after returning to Mankranso from the meeting but could not survive. In the past week, his district has been in the news spotlight after he was accused of spearheading an attempt to demolish a school facility at Mankranso to pave the way for the construction of a 24-hour economy market. He denied the allegation. Mr Sedik was the NDC parliamentary candidate for the area in the 2024 election.

items.title: Sebta : Madrid surveille les appels à une nouvelle entrée collective et maintient le contact avec Rabat
items.description: Les autorités espagnoles suivent de près les appels diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux en faveur d’une nouvelle tentative d’entrée collective à Sebta occupée, annoncée pour le 23 septembre, jour des élections législatives au Maroc. Madrid affirme avoir renforcé son dispositif préventif et maintient, dans le même temps, des échanges réguliers avec les autorités marocaines sur la gestion de la frontière et le retour des migrants en situation irrégulière. Le ministre espagnol des Affaires étrangères, de l’Union européenne et de la Coopération, José Manuel Albares, a assuré que les autorités espagnoles ne considéraient pas, à ce stade, que les appels relayés sur les réseaux sociaux bénéficiaient d’une adhésion comparable à celle observée lors d’un précédent épisode. Selon le responsable espagnol, les messages appelant à une nouvelle tentative d’entrée à Sebta occupée « ne suscitent pas, jusqu’à présent, de réponse parmi la population » et leur impact serait inférieur à celui de la mobilisation annoncée le 30 juillet dernier. Albares a notamment fait référence à la circulation de fausses informations autour d’une décision de la Cour suprême espagnole relative aux conditions de renvoi des migrants entrés à la nage. Face à la circulation de ces contenus, Madrid a activé un dispositif destiné à lutter contre la désinformation. Le ministre a indiqué que les consulats espagnols ainsi que l’ambassade à Rabat diffusent des informations destinées à rappeler que l’entrée irrégulière à Sebta et Melilla n’ouvre pas, selon les autorités espagnoles, un droit au séjour en Espagne ou dans l’Union européenne. Madrid renforce son dispositif et mise sur la prévention Albares a également appelé les personnes susceptibles d’envisager une tentative d’entrée irrégulière à ne pas mettre en jeu leurs ressources ou leur avenir en se fiant aux réseaux de passeurs et aux informations diffusées en ligne. Les représentations diplomatiques espagnoles au Maroc seraient, selon lui, également en contact avec la presse marocaine afin de faire circuler des informations considérées comme fiables sur les conditions d’accès aux deux présides occupés. Cette stratégie de prévention accompagne un renforcement du dispositif de sécurité à la frontière. Le ministre espagnol a assuré que son gouvernement travaillait parallèlement avec Rabat afin de prévenir toute nouvelle tentative de passage collectif. Le contact avec les autorités marocaines porte également sur la question du retour des migrants. Albares a fait état d’une communication « constante » avec le ministère marocain des Affaires étrangères afin de traiter les dossiers de retour une fois les procédures nécessaires préparées. Le responsable espagnol a par ailleurs évoqué le précédent du 15 août, lorsqu’une tentative d’entrée collective avait, selon Madrid, échoué. Il attribue ce résultat notamment à l’action menée contre la désinformation et au renforcement des forces déployées au niveau de la frontière. Cette coopération entre Madrid et Rabat intervient alors que la question migratoire demeure un volet important des relations entre le Maroc, l’Espagne et l’Union européenne. Pour les autorités espagnoles, la prévention des arrivées irrégulières repose notamment sur le contrôle des frontières, la lutte contre les réseaux de trafic de migrants et les mécanismes de retour et de réadmission. Bruxelles confirme son soutien à la coopération migratoire La Commission européenne a, de son côté, rappelé le soutien financier et logistique apporté à l’Espagne pour la protection de ses frontières et la gestion des opérations de retour, dans le contexte des arrivées irrégulières enregistrées à Sebta depuis le Maroc. Bruxelles considère également le Maroc comme un partenaire important dans les domaines de la migration et de la gestion des frontières. Dans des réponses apportées au Parlement européen sur les financements accordés au Royaume, la Commission souligne que l’aide européenne vise notamment à renforcer les capacités marocaines de contrôle des frontières et de lutte contre le trafic de migrants. Selon la Commission, cette coopération a déjà produit des résultats avec une baisse importante des arrivées irrégulières. Elle précise toutefois que des discussions restent en cours avec les autorités marocaines afin de développer davantage le partenariat dans le domaine migratoire, particulièrement sur les questions de retour et de réadmission. Ces échanges s’inscrivent dans des négociations plus larges visant, selon Bruxelles, à parvenir à un partenariat « global et stratégique » avec le Maroc en matière de migration. items.title: Ghanaian professor Kofi Akamani shot dead in US; wife arrested
items.description: A Ghanaian academic based in the United States, Dr Kofi Akamani, has been shot dead in Illinois, where he worked as a lecturer at Southern Illinois University (SIU) Carbondale. The 48-year-old was fatally wounded in a shooting reported near Lake Road, between Murphysboro and Carbondale, at about 5 p.m. on Saturday. The Jackson County Sheriff’s Office said deputies who responded to the scene found Akamani injured, and he was subsequently taken to Memorial Hospital of Carbondale, where he was pronounced dead. Dr Akamani was a professor in SIU Carbondale’s Department of Forestry, where he taught subjects including forest recreation and conservation social science. His death has triggered an investigation by the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office, which said his 35-year-old wife, Betty Akamani, had been arrested in connection with the incident and was facing multiple charges. Authorities said the circumstances surrounding the shooting remain under investigation and cautioned that the case was still in its early stages. The Jackson County Ambulance Service, Jackson County Coroner’s Office and Jackson County State’s Attorney’s Office assisted the sheriff’s office with the investigation. No further details have been released by authorities. Dr Akamani’s academic journey began in Ghana at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he earned a Bachelor of Science in Development Planning with a specialisation in Urban Planning. He later obtained an MPhil from the University of Oslo’s Centre for Development and the Environment in 2006 before earning a PhD in Natural Resources from the University of Idaho. During his doctoral studies, he returned to Ghana for six months to research collaborative forest management and its impact on the social and ecological resilience of two forest-dependent communities in the Ashanti Region.
