items.title: What is left of Maspero after national broadcaster’s debt-for-assets swap?
items.description: The National Broadcasting Authority — known by the name of its Downtown headquarters, Maspero — has been weighed down by debt for decades, borrowing heavily from the National Investment Bank (NIB) as it has struggled to maintain a leading role as state broadcaster and production house in a changing media scene, grappling initially with the move to satellite, and now to digital media. All of that accumulated debt, worth a total of around LE139.7 billion, was settled at the end of August, in a single assets-for-debt swap, with the Planning Ministry announcing that the ownership of 44 assets, unused by the broadcasting authority and worth around LE18.06 billion, including land and buildings, would be transferred to the NIB. What the assets are, how they were valued and what will happen to them going forward remains unclear. While sources speaking to Mada Masr pointed to some of the land assets that are owned by the company and indicated some of those included in the deal, they were not aware of how these lands will be leveraged for investment going forward. The move, however, eliminates debts that Maspero has been racking up since the 1980s as the state has, simultaneously, withdrawn its investments from its traditional media vehicles and focused instead on United Media Services (UMS). The ministry has said that the step was taken in line with a broader move to resolve the historical debts of government entities and authorities, part of what it called “the political leadership’s directives.” In this light, the Maspero debt-for-assets swap marks a major step toward implementation of plans the prime minister announced at the beginning of the year to resolve the huge amount of government debt, leveraging state assets and land for investment to write off public borrowing as part of the continuing process of shaping President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s “New Republic.” How was the deal announced? The swap was announced on August 26 as part of a framework agreement signed by the Finance and Planning Ministers, with the heads of NIB and Maspero. The Cabinet initially announced that the total debts were LE88.3 billion, with the Planning Ministry elaborating the following day to state that the total debts resolved amounted to LE139.7 billion, including LE51.4 billion that were written off entirely and that included accumulated interest and late-payment penalties owed by the broadcasting authority. The remaining LE70.24 billion would be repaid by the state, according to the ministry, through the allocation of land to the bank, with the aim of increasing the bank’s asset base and enabling it to redeploy those assets in national projects that would create more jobs — something the ministry referred to as another form of government support for debt settlement. The file was to be fully closed, the Planning Ministry stated, and the accumulation of any new late-payment penalties halted as of July 1 until completion of the settlement procedures. What remains of Maspero? A broadcaster, a senior specialist at the National Broadcasting Authority and a news program director, tell Mada Masr in separate statements that the debt settlement agreement remained unclear and that there was a lack of transparency over how the 44 plots of land belonging to Maspero were valued at LE18 billion. The broadcaster and the director both believe that the government has not disclosed the size or locations of the relinquished land so as not to expose its unfair valuation. According to the broadcaster, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, the state allocated vast areas of land to the authority since the launch of state television in the 1960s t o ensure strong transmission coverage in every region, with every governorate having at least one television transmission center. From television’s beginnings until the year 2000, dozens of presidential decrees allocated state land in different governorates for the construction of radio and television transmission stations and transferred them, free of charge, to the Egyptian Radio and Television Union (ETRU) — the entity headquartered at Maspero that would later become the National Broadcasting Authority. According to the news-department director, who spoke to Mada Masr on the condition of anonymity, Maspero owns between 3,000 and 4,500 feddans of land distributed across Sharm el-Sheikh — specifically Umm al-Sid Plateau — the Agouza area and Faisal Street in Giza Governorate, Sharqiya, Minya near Gabel al-Tayr and Zaafarana on the Red Sea coast. It also owns a small plot in the New Capital, the equivalent of no more than three feddans, surrounding a small news studio built out of funding for the capital. The broadcaster added that the authority also owns large areas in Moqattam and Abu Zaabal in Cairo, as well as substantial land in Marsa Matrouh and North and South Sinai. A third source working for a private-sector asset consulting and valuation firm said that one of the most important plots included in the debt settlement is land in Zaafarana formerly owned by the ERTU. Other plots in various areas — including Helwan in Cairo, Fayoum and Upper Egypt — were also part of the agreement. The broadcaster says that information about the settlement also indicates that ownership of radio and television transmission stations would be transferred to the bank, with the exception of the radio and television transmission station in Moqattam, the old media club’s land at the entrance to Moqattam’s upper plateau and the radio building on the Sherifeen Street in the Egyptian Exchange area of Downtown Cairo. According to an informed Housing Ministry source, the studios and staff currently housed in Downtown Cairo’s Maspero building will be moved in full to the new global studios city, planned for the Dahshur area, south of the Giza Plateau. The facility is intended to be used for filming and as a tourist attraction, as part of a project to develop the surroundings of the archaeological Giza Pyramids area. The source says the project was approved by the Cabinet in December 2025 after the international consultancy Wimberly, Allison, Tong & Goo (WATG) was commissioned to prepare its master plan. In its statement on the financial details of the settlement, the Planning Ministry said the inventory process had been conducted with “extreme care” to ensure that no “revenue-generating” assets owned by the authority were affected, in order to preserve its financial position and sustainability. The statement specifically referred to the authority’s shares in satellite operator Nilesat and the Egyptian Media Production City (EMPC), which had already been pledged to the NIB. Those shares are to be fully released once the agreed asset transfers are completed. The government assured that the debt settlement would still allow Maspero to benefit from the returns on its shares in Nilesat and the EMPC. The agreement itself did not specify the worth of the shares, nor the broadcasting authority’s ownership percentage in the two companies. In a subsequent move after the settlement was finalized, the broadcasting authority announced that it owns approximately 40 percent of Nilesat and 45 percent of the EMPC. A quarter century of debt In 2021, the broadcasting authority stated it had not received any loans from the NIB since its establishment, explaining that any debts owed to the bank were not incurred by the authority itself since its creation, but were debts that had been transferred to it when it replaced the former ERTU. Those debts included LE9.6 billion in loans from the NIB, dating back to 1981, on which interest had reached LE32.9 billion by then, bringing total accumulated debt to LE42.6 billion. So, how did the ERTU become so mired in debt? “Maspero was deliberately drowned in debt over the years,” the broadcaster says. She describes a decline in the credibility of state television after the 20 11 revolution, which resulted from the misguided policies of successive administrations, she says, and coincided with the rise of UMS as an alternative, depriving Maspero of its audience, and, consequently, its ability to generate revenue and self-finance. Maspero’s debts began to accumulate when Safwat al-Sherif became Information Minister in 1982. During the tenures of Sherif and Anas al-Fekky, television underwent massive expansion, including the launch of Nilesat, the establishment of the EMPC, the creation of dozens of specialized and regional channels and the modernization of studios and purchase of equipment. Most of these expansions and investment needs were financed through loans from the NIB, at a time when Egyptian television enjoyed significant institutional prestige, and, according to the broadcaster, when no one dared interfere with it. Indicating the decree of expansion, the broadcaster notes that during this period, the number of employees at the ERTU expanded to between 40,000 and 45,000, causing annual wage and pension costs to surpass LE2.5 billion. At the same time, Maspero’s revenues declined as the satellite television market was liberalized and private channels expanded from the beginning of the new millennium. A large share of advertisers and viewers shifted to competing channels, reducing Maspero’s share in the advertising market. Maspero’s production sector, alongside Sono Cairo and the EMPC, used to enjoy a role as the backbone of Egyptian drama from the 1960s until 2010, when Egyptian television produced, financed and broadcast its own works. But the ERTU’s financial collapse and mounting debts to the NIB gradually deprived it of its ability to finance production. As documented by the Central Auditing Organization in a 2016 report , ETRU contracted work out to executive producers and co-producers, financing productions for third parties despite owning the studios and personnel, until its production sector stopped producing television series altogether in 2016. Private production companies and Gulf channels initially filled the gap. Since 2018, however, the role has been assumed by UMS, which acquired major production arms, including Synergy and Media Hub, among others, as well as broadcasting channels such as ONtv, DMC network and Al-Hayah. It consequently came to dominate the production and distribution of the majority of Ramadan television series, while Maspero shifted from being a producer to merely a broadcaster that acquired UMS’s productions under broadcast agreements. The broadcaster explains that in recent years, the drama and programming production role previously performed by Maspero specifically shifted to UMS, which is owned by sovereign entities through The Sovereign Fund of Egypt and Eagle Capital for Financial Investments, a private equity fund owned by the General Intelligence Services. The company now produces a vast array of content and broadcasts these on a variety of channels that are able to operate as private sector companies. Maspero’s role in news also gradually diminished. Since UMS’s acquisition of most private media outlets in Egypt in 2019, the company — through eXtra News, which came under its control, and then Al-Qahera News, launched in November 2022 — has become the state’s de-facto news arm. Meanwhile, Maspero’s Nile News channel, a part of its news sector, has been reduced to broadcasting conventional bulletins and official coverage, without a field correspondent network or modern production resources. Maspero, therefore, no longer earned revenues from producing drama, exclusive broadcasting or radio rights for certain sporting events, particularly as state investment became concentrated in UMS. The director in Maspero’s news sector, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, says Maspero had been stripped of the revenues from sports broadcasting rights, which had generated substantial income, even though matches continued to be broadcast on its channels. “We do not know how UMS acquired the broadcasting rights or under what agreement,” they say. Egyptian television was the exclusive broadcaster of Egyptian Premier League matches until mid-2017. Its last major contract with the Egyptian Football Association, signed in January 2014, was worth LE70 million per season. In the 2017/18 season, the rights passed to Presentation Sports Agency, which took over marketing rights for the league, the Egypt Cup and s major clubs, and assigned broadcasting to ON Sport channels. The entire system then passed to the UMS in 2019 through ON Time Sports, and Maspero exited the sports broadcasting market entirely. Rights values have since risen far beyond the value of Maspero’s contracts. The Egyptian Professional Football Clubs Association announced in June 2026 that broadcasting and commercial rights contracts had increased by 300 percent over four seasons, with the new revenue and prize package reaching LE1 billion, while the value of UMS’ own contracts remained officially undisclosed. The director added that the National Broadcasting Authority’s remaining resources had become almost symbolic, consisting mainly of government advertising and awareness campaigns supposedly intended for state television, as well as radio car licensing fees that the Interior Ministry is expected to remit to the authority. Owners of cars equipped with electronic or entertainment systems pay an annual fee of LE100, 40 percent of which is allocated to the broadcasting authority — a charge commonly known in the media as the “radio tax.” As the broadcasting authority’s installments continued to go unpaid, interest and late-payment penalties accumulated on the principal debt over the years. In the August settlement, the Planning Ministry stated that approximately LE51.4 billion in interest and late-payment penalties was written off, including LE45 billion in late-payment penalties and LE6.4 billion in interest. Interest and penalties therefore accounted for a substantial share of the total debt, rather than the loans’ principal alone. In addition to the debt burden, reports issued by the Central Auditing Organization over the years documented financial and administrative violations, as well as shortcomings in the management and use of some assets owned by the ERTU, that were estimated to be worth billions of Egyptian pounds before some of them were transferred to the National Broadcasting Authority. Both the broadcaster and the news director say that instead of addressing the process through which Maspero was saddled with debt, and reforming it administratively by making use of its assets, the authority was being stripped of those assets. This has raised concerns among employees that new debts could accumulate and eventually lead to the complete liquidation of the authority’s role. Economic advisor and capital markets expert Wael al-Nahhas supports the sources’ view. He describes the Maspero debt settlement as tantamount to liquidating the institution, saying that with Maspero’s resources depleted and its real estate assets stripped away, its continued existence is merely a matter of time. Nahhas says that in 2015, he had worked with officials inside state agencies on a plan to settle Maspero’s debts by investing its assets in a way that would ensure sustainable revenues and keep it functioning. He explains that it involved using Maspero’s land in prime locations to build world-class studios that could be rented to international news agencies, alongside media projects that would generate income, enabling it to develop its resources and continue operating. The plan, however, ran into laws prohibiting the disposal of land designated for public benefit. Nahhas points out that the settlement recently announced by the government is based on stripping Maspero — and other state institutions indebted to the NIB — of their real estate assets so that the government can continue borrowing. He said that Maspero needs approximately LE20 billion annually, at least, to continue its activities, but that it receives only enough to cover employee salaries from the state budget, which the director and media professional estimate to be around LE220 million per month. Its continued operation amid such scarce resources is therefore “impossible.” According to the broadcaster, Maspero’s workforce has shrunk from 42,000 employees since 2010 to just 15,000 today, after between 60 and 70 percent of its employees retired. She said the average age of current employees is around 50 and expect the next step to be, once outstanding end-of-service payments and financial differences are settled, the introduction of an early-retirement scheme at age 55. She believes this would be welcomed by a large proportion of employees who were replaced by the UMS staff when the company supervised work in the news sector in recent years. The broadcaster and news director said Maspero employees had been told that the deal would be followed by progress on delayed end-of-service benefits and pension payments. Between 6,000 and 7,000 retirees reportedly have unpaid entitlements dating back to 2019, while current employees’ salaries have been frozen since 2014 and bonuses have gone unpaid for approximately 70 months. Debt write-offs in exchange for assets The National Broadcasting Authority — known by the name of its Downtown headquarters, Maspero — has been weighed down by debt for decades, borrowing heavily from the National Investment Bank (NIB) as it has struggled to maintain a leading role as state broadcaster and production house in a changing media scene, grappling initially with the move to satellite, and now to digital media. All of that accumulated debt, worth a total of around LE139.7 billion, was settled at the end of August, in a single assets-for-debt swap, with the Planning Ministry announcing that the ownership of 44 assets, unused by the broadcasting authority and worth around LE18.06 billion, including land and buildings, would be transferred to the NIB. What the assets are, how they were valued and what will happen to them going forward remains unclear. While sources speaking to Mada Masr pointed to some of the land assets that are owned by the company and indicated some of those included in the deal, they were not aware of how these lands will be leveraged for investment going forward. The move, however, eliminates debts that Maspero has been racking up since the 1980s as the state has, simultaneously, withdrawn its investments from its traditional media vehicles and focused instead on United Media Services (UMS). The ministry has said that the step was taken in line with a broader move to resolve the historical debts of government entities and authorities, part of what it called “the political leadership’s directives.” In this light, the Maspero debt-for-assets swap marks a major step toward implementation of plans the prime minister announced at the beginning of the year to resolve the huge amount of government debt, leveraging state assets and land for investment to write off public borrowing as part of the continuing process of shaping President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s “New Republic.” How was the deal announced? The swap was announced on August 26 as part of a framework agreement signed by the Finance and Planning Ministers, with the heads of NIB and Maspero. The Cabinet initially announced that the total debts were LE88.3 billion, with the Planning Ministry elaborating the following day to state that the total debts resolved amounted to LE139.7 billion, including LE51.4 billion that were written off entirely and that included accumulated interest and late-payment penalties owed by the broadcasting authority. The remaining LE70.24 billion would be repaid by the state, according to the ministry, through the allocation of land to the bank, with the aim of increasing the bank’s asset base and enabling it to redeploy those assets in national projects that would create more jobs — something the ministry referred to as another form of government support for debt settlement. The file was to be fully closed, the Planning Ministry stated, and the accumulation of any new late-payment penalties halted as of July 1 until completion of the settlement procedures. What remains of Maspero? A broadcaster, a senior specialist at the National Broadcasting Authority and a news program director, tell Mada Masr in separate statements that the debt settlement agreement remained unclear and that there was a lack of transparency over how the 44 plots of land belonging to Maspero were valued at LE18 billion. The broadcaster and the director both believe that the government has not disclosed the size or locations of the relinquished land so as not to expose its unfair valuation. According to the broadcaster, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, the state allocated vast areas of land to the authority since the launch of state television in the 1960s t o ensure strong transmission coverage in every region, with every governorate having at least one television transmission center. From television’s beginnings until the year 2000, dozens of presidential decrees allocated state land in different governorates for the construction of radio and television transmission stations and transferred them, free of charge, to the Egyptian Radio and Television Union (ETRU) — the entity headquartered at Maspero that would later become the National Broadcasting Authority. According to the news-department director, who spoke to Mada Masr on the condition of anonymity, Maspero owns between 3,000 and 4,500 feddans of land distributed across Sharm el-Sheikh — specifically Umm al-Sid Plateau — the Agouza area and Faisal Street in Giza Governorate, Sharqiya, Minya near Gabel al-Tayr and Zaafarana on the Red Sea coast. It also owns a small plot in the New Capital, the equivalent of no more than three feddans, surrounding a small news studio built out of funding for the capital. The broadcaster added that the authority also owns large areas in Moqattam and Abu Zaabal in Cairo, as well as substantial land in Marsa Matrouh and North and South Sinai. A third source working for a private-sector asset consulting and valuation firm said that one of the most important plots included in the debt settlement is land in Zaafarana formerly owned by the ERTU. Other plots in various areas — including Helwan in Cairo, Fayoum and Upper Egypt — were also part of the agreement. The broadcaster says that information about the settlement also indicates that ownership of radio and television transmission stations would be transferred to the bank, with the exception of the radio and television transmission station in Moqattam, the old media club’s land at the entrance to Moqattam’s upper plateau and the radio building on the Sherifeen Street in the Egyptian Exchange area of Downtown Cairo. According to an informed Housing Ministry source, the studios and staff currently housed in Downtown Cairo’s Maspero building will be moved in full to the new global studios city, planned for the Dahshur area, south of the Giza Plateau. The facility is intended to be used for filming and as a tourist attraction, as part of a project to develop the surroundings of the archaeological Giza Pyramids area. The source says the project was approved by the Cabinet in December 2025 after the international consultancy Wimberly, Allison, Tong & Goo (WATG) was commissioned to prepare its master plan. In its statement on the financial details of the settlement, the Planning Ministry said the inventory process had been conducted with “extreme care” to ensure that no “revenue-generating” assets owned by the authority were affected, in order to preserve its financial position and sustainability. The statement specifically referred to the authority’s shares in satellite operator Nilesat and the Egyptian Media Production City (EMPC), which had already been pledged to the NIB. Those shares are to be fully released once the agreed asset transfers are completed. The government assured that the debt settlement would still allow Maspero to benefit from the returns on its shares in Nilesat and the EMPC. The agreement itself did not specify the worth of the shares, nor the broadcasting authority’s ownership percentage in the two companies. In a subsequent move after the settlement was finalized, the broadcasting authority announced that it owns approximately 40 percent of Nilesat and 45 percent of the EMPC. A quarter century of debt In 2021, the broadcasting authority stated it had not received any loans from the NIB since its establishment, explaining that any debts owed to the bank were not incurred by the authority itself since its creation, but were debts that had been transferred to it when it replaced the former ERTU. Those debts included LE9.6 billion in loans from the NIB, dating back to 1981, on which interest had reached LE32.9 billion by then, bringing total accumulated debt to LE42.6 billion. So, how did the ERTU become so mired in debt? “Maspero was deliberately drowned in debt over the years,” the broadcaster says. She describes a decline in the credibility of state television after the 20 11 revolution, which resulted from the misguided policies of successive administrations, she says, and coincided with the rise of UMS as an alternative, depriving Maspero of its audience, and, consequently, its ability to generate revenue and self-finance. Maspero’s debts began to accumulate when Safwat al-Sherif became Information Minister in 1982. During the tenures of Sherif and Anas al-Fekky, television underwent massive expansion, including the launch of Nilesat, the establishment of the EMPC, the creation of dozens of specialized and regional channels and the modernization of studios and purchase of equipment. Most of these expansions and investment needs were financed through loans from the NIB, at a time when Egyptian television enjoyed significant institutional prestige, and, according to the broadcaster, when no one dared interfere with it. Indicating the decree of expansion, the broadcaster notes that during this period, the number of employees at the ERTU expanded to between 40,000 and 45,000, causing annual wage and pension costs to surpass LE2.5 billion. At the same time, Maspero’s revenues declined as the satellite television market was liberalized and private channels expanded from the beginning of the new millennium. A large share of advertisers and viewers shifted to competing channels, reducing Maspero’s share in the advertising market. Maspero’s production sector, alongside Sono Cairo and the EMPC, used to enjoy a role as the backbone of Egyptian drama from the 1960s until 2010, when Egyptian television produced, financed and broadcast its own works. But the ERTU’s financial collapse and mounting debts to the NIB gradually deprived it of its ability to finance production. As documented by the Central Auditing Organization in a 2016 report , ETRU contracted work out to executive producers and co-producers, financing productions for third parties despite owning the studios and personnel, until its production sector stopped producing television series altogether in 2016. Private production companies and Gulf channels initially filled the gap. Since 2018, however, the role has been assumed by UMS, which acquired major production arms, including Synergy and Media Hub, among others, as well as broadcasting channels such as ONtv, DMC network and Al-Hayah. It consequently came to dominate the production and distribution of the majority of Ramadan television series, while Maspero shifted from being a producer to merely a broadcaster that acquired UMS’s productions under broadcast agreements. The broadcaster explains that in recent years, the drama and programming production role previously performed by Maspero specifically shifted to UMS, which is owned by sovereign entities through The Sovereign Fund of Egypt and Eagle Capital for Financial Investments, a private equity fund owned by the General Intelligence Services. The company now produces a vast array of content and broadcasts these on a variety of channels that are able to operate as private sector companies. Maspero’s role in news also gradually diminished. Since UMS’s acquisition of most private media outlets in Egypt in 2019, the company — through eXtra News, which came under its control, and then Al-Qahera News, launched in November 2022 — has become the state’s de-facto news arm. Meanwhile, Maspero’s Nile News channel, a part of its news sector, has been reduced to broadcasting conventional bulletins and official coverage, without a field correspondent network or modern production resources. Maspero, therefore, no longer earned revenues from producing drama, exclusive broadcasting or radio rights for certain sporting events, particularly as state investment became concentrated in UMS. The director in Maspero’s news sector, who also spoke on condition of anonymity, says Maspero had been stripped of the revenues from sports broadcasting rights, which had generated substantial income, even though matches continued to be broadcast on its channels. “We do not know how UMS acquired the broadcasting rights or under what agreement,” they say. Egyptian television was the exclusive broadcaster of Egyptian Premier League matches until mid-2017. Its last major contract with the Egyptian Football Association, signed in January 2014, was worth LE70 million per season. In the 2017/18 season, the rights passed to Presentation Sports Agency, which took over marketing rights for the league, the Egypt Cup and s major clubs, and assigned broadcasting to ON Sport channels. The entire system then passed to the UMS in 2019 through ON Time Sports, and Maspero exited the sports broadcasting market entirely. Rights values have since risen far beyond the value of Maspero’s contracts. The Egyptian Professional Football Clubs Association announced in June 2026 that broadcasting and commercial rights contracts had increased by 300 percent over four seasons, with the new revenue and prize package reaching LE1 billion, while the value of UMS’ own contracts remained officially undisclosed. The director added that the National Broadcasting Authority’s remaining resources had become almost symbolic, consisting mainly of government advertising and awareness campaigns supposedly intended for state television, as well as radio car licensing fees that the Interior Ministry is expected to remit to the authority. Owners of cars equipped with electronic or entertainment systems pay an annual fee of LE100, 40 percent of which is allocated to the broadcasting authority — a charge commonly known in the media as the “radio tax.” As the broadcasting authority’s installments continued to go unpaid, interest and late-payment penalties accumulated on the principal debt over the years. In the August settlement, the Planning Ministry stated that approximately LE51.4 billion in interest and late-payment penalties was written off, including LE45 billion in late-payment penalties and LE6.4 billion in interest. Interest and penalties therefore accounted for a substantial share of the total debt, rather than the loans’ principal alone. In addition to the debt burden, reports issued by the Central Auditing Organization over the years documented financial and administrative violations, as well as shortcomings in the management and use of some assets owned by the ERTU, that were estimated to be worth billions of Egyptian pounds before some of them were transferred to the National Broadcasting Authority. Both the broadcaster and the news director say that instead of addressing the process through which Maspero was saddled with debt, and reforming it administratively by making use of its assets, the authority was being stripped of those assets. The NIB is a state-owned bank established by former President Anwar al-Sadat in 1980 and affiliated with the Planning Ministry. It is not a commercial bank: it does not open accounts for individuals or provide conventional banking services. Rather, it is a sovereign financing institution tasked with funding investment projects included in the state’s economic and social development plan. The accumulation of domestic debt — the total amount borrowed in local currency by the government, economic authorities and public entities from within the national economy — is linked to the expansion of state spending and growing financing needs. Its trajectory, however, has accelerated upward since 2011, alongside widening budget deficits and declining sources of revenue. Domestic debt stood at approximately between LE800 and LE900 billion before 2011, exceeded LE2 trillion by 2015 and approached LE4 trillion in 2019, before continuing to rise in subsequent years amid increasing financing needs, higher interest rates and the depreciation of the local currency. By 2025, domestic debt had exceeded LE12 trillion, representing a high proportion of GDP. The bulk of domestic debt consists of government debt instruments, particularly treasury bills and bonds subscribed to by the banking sector and local investors, alongside intergovernmental balances and debts, including the government’s debt to the NIB. Its main problems include the high debt-servicing costs, as interest payments consume a large share of public spending, limiting the resources available for other sectors and services. Deficit and debt financing can also have inflationary effects, particularly when it involves monetary expansion or direct financing by the central bank. Another challenge is the potential crowding out of the private sector, as rising government financing needs may absorb a larger share of the liquidity available in the banking system, limiting financing for private and productive investment. The National Investment Bank took assets equivalent to the debt and will develop and operate them.” He added: “Remove the word ‘Maspero’ and replace it with ‘the state’; remove ‘National Investment Bank’ and replace it with ‘the central bank’; remove ‘land’ and replace it with ownership stakes in state-owned companies or even the Suez Canal — and that amounts to eliminating domestic public debt.” These ideas sparked widespread public anger over fears that sovereign state assets, such as the Suez Canal, could be relinquished from sovereign control and sold off to investors, particularly amid growing Gulf investor interest in Egyptian assets. items.title: Le secrétaire général de l’ONU plaide pour que les richesses de l’Afrique profitent aux Africains
items.description: L’Afrique dispose d’importants atouts pour s’imposer dans l’économie mondiale. Mais pour le Secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, le continent doit désormais rompre avec le modèle consistant à exporter ses matières premières sans suffisamment bénéficier de leur transformation et de la valeur créée. « Plus de pillage », a lancé António Guterres dimanche à New […] L’article Le secrétaire général de l'ONU plaide pour que les richesses de l'Afrique profitent aux Africains est apparu en premier sur Tchadinfos .

items.title: Tourisme: les agences de voyages marocaines confrontées au calme plat de l'automne
items.description: La saison automnale reste hors du « circuit de prospérité » pour les agences de voyages marocaines, en raison de la concentration de la demande sur leurs services durant les vacances saisonnières, avec à leur tête la saison estivale qui connaît un engouement plus important des Marocains pour les voyages à l'étranger. Cette situation intervient au moment où les destinations touristiques mondiales s'apprêtent à accueillir des flux de voyageurs au cours de l'automne, qui débute au début de la semaine prochaine, en lançant des offres de voyage adaptées à la nature de cette saison de l'année. Mohamed Semlali, président de la Fédération nationale des agences de voyages du Maroc (FNAV), a confirmé que « la saison automnale enregistre chaque année les niveaux de demande les plus bas pour les programmes touristiques proposés par les agences marocaines vers l'étranger, ainsi que pour les services de billetterie aérienne ». Semlali a expliqué, dans une déclaration à Hespress , que « le repli qui accompagne chaque saison automnale est principalement dû à sa coïncidence directe avec la rentrée scolaire et la fin des vacances d'été, ce qui contraint les familles marocaines à réorienter leurs budgets vers les dépenses d'enseignement et les engagements familiaux, faisant du voyage une option exclue pour elles ». L'intervenant a poursuivi en précisant que « même les destinations européennes proches comme l'Espagne et le Portugal, qui se positionnent comme des options touristiques durant la période automnale, n'attirent pas les voyageurs via les programmes des agences de voyages ; la majorité des Marocains préférant organiser leur voyage de manière indépendante et acheter leurs billets directement, loin des offres combinées proposées par les agences durant cette saison » . Le même acteur a souligné que « les choix de voyage en automne se compliquent davantage sous la pression des contraintes économiques mondiales et des tensions régionales, qui contribuent à instaurer un état d'hésitation générale chez les citoyens quant à la planification de voyages à l'étranger » . Il a ajouté : « Même certaines destinations asiatiques qui constituaient une échappatoire à certaines périodes, comme la Thaïlande, ont connu des changements suite à la suspension de l'exemption de visa de soixante jours pour les Marocains » , notant que « les vacances saisonnières continuent de régir la mobilité des touristes marocains vers l'étranger » . S'agissant de l'activité des agents de voyages marocains, Semlali a indiqué que « la prolifération des plateformes et sites étrangers de réservation de billets d'avion et d'hébergement hôtelier constitue le défi le plus majeur pour les agences de voyages dans le Royaume, ces plateformes ayant accaparé une part importante du marché, ce qui a rendu les voyageurs marocains vers l'étranger, dans de nombreux cas, autonomes vis-à-vis des acteurs du secteur dans le pays » . Dans un contexte connexe, la saison automnale permet au Maroc de diversifier son produit et son offre touristique, compte tenu de la douceur des températures dans plusieurs régions et de la baisse de la fréquentation par rapport aux mois d'été. Le Maroc connaît, entre les mois de septembre et novembre de chaque année, ce que l'on appelle la « mi-saison » (Shoulder Season), qui attire les visiteurs à la recherche d'un climat plus doux et d'une atmosphère moins encombrée. The post Tourisme: les agences de voyages marocaines confrontées au calme plat de l'automne appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Diphtérie : 11 décès dus à l’épidémie
items.description: Au total, 11 décès ont été enregistrés le 20 septembre à travers les 31 districts sanitaires, touchés par la diphtérie. C’est ce qui ressort du point fait lundi par le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique. Onze décès ont été causés par l’épidémie de la diphtérie depuis le 1er août, date à laquelle le premier cas est apparu. Le point de la situation au 20 septembre fait état de 114 cas qui ont été confirmés à travers les 31 districts sanitaires répartis dans 12 régions. La région de Kédougou compte 33 cas (kédougou 23, Saraya 8 et Salémata 2 cas), Louga 16 cas (kébémer 6, Darou-Mousty 8, Sakal et Louga chacun 1 cas) et Dakar 15 cas (Guédiawaye 7, Keur Massar 3 et Dakar-Ouest, Dakar-Nord, Dakar-Sud, Pikine et Sangalkam chacun 1 cas). Sous la barre des 15 cas : la région de Thiès a enregistré 12 cas (Mbour 11 et Thiadiaye 1 cas), Diourbel 13 cas (Touba 12 et Mbacké 1 cas) et Matam 6 cas (le département de Matam 5 et Thilogne 1 cas). A lire aussi : Diphtérie au Sénégal : le bilan grimpe à 57 cas confirmés et 8 décès, Kédougou toujours en première ligne L’épidémie a infecté 5 personnes à Kaolack (Kaolack 1, Guinguinéo 2 et Ndoffane 2 cas) et Tambacounda compte également 5 cas confirmés (dont 4 à Bakel et 1 à Diankhé-makha). Le ministère de la Santé a déclaré 4 cas à Kolda (les 4 à Vélingara), 2 cas à Saint-Louis (1 à Saint-Louis et l’autre à Dagana), 2 cas à Ziguinchor (répartis entre Bignona et Ziguinchor) et 1 cas à Fatick. Le ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique rappelle que la « diphtérie est une maladie infectieuse et contagieuse mais évitable grâce à la vaccination ». Il invite ainsi les parents à respecter le calendrier vaccinal du Programme élargi de vaccination. L’épidémie peut se manifester entre autres par un mal de gorge, de la fièvre, une difficulté à avaler, un enrouement et un gonflement du cou. La diphtérie peut aussi entraîner la présence de membranes grisâtres dans la gorge, causant des difficultés respiratoires. Boubacar DIOP (Stagiaire)

items.title: De la cocaïne cachée dans deux camions citernes saisie à Tamanrasset
items.description: Une importante quantité de cocaïne a été saisie ce lundi par les forces de l’ANP à Tamanrasset dans l’extrême sud du pays, a annoncé le ministère de la Défense nationale dans un communiqué. Deux narcotrafiquants ont été arrêtés lors de cette opération. « Dans le cadre des efforts continus déployés pour sécuriser les frontières nationales et lutter contre les barons de la contrebande et le crime organisé, et grâce à une utilisation optimale du renseignement, des détachements conjoints de l'Armée nationale populaire du secteur militaire de Tamanrasset ont réussi ce lundi 21 septembre 2026 à arrêter deux trafiquants de drogue et à saisir une importante quantité de cocaïne, estimée à plus de 58 kilogrammes », a indiqué le MDN. La cocaïne était cachée dans deux camions citernes La cocaïne était « soigneusement dissimulée dans deux camions citernes », a précisé la même source. « Cette opération confirme la pleine capacité opérationnelle de toutes les composantes de l'Armée nationale populaire à faire face à toute tentative d'inonder le pays de stupéfiants et de porter atteinte à la sécurité des citoyens », a conclu le MDN. L’Algérie a décidé de créer un organisme sécuritaire spécialisé dans la lutte contre le trafic de drogue sur le modèle de la DEA américaine, et de transformer une caserne militaire dans le désert de Tanezrouft en prison de haute sécurité pour les narcotrafiquants. items.title: Rentrée scolaire 2026 : l’Intersyndicale de l’éducation pose ses conditions avant tout recrutement
items.description: L’Intersyndicale de l’éducation, composée du Syndicat national de l’éducation (SNE), du Syndicat libre des enseignants-chercheurs de Guinée (SLECG) et de la Fédération syndicale des professionnels de l’éducation (FSPE), a animé un point de presse ce lundi 21 septembre à Dixinn. Au cœur des échanges : le recrutement des enseignants annoncé par le ministère de la Fonction publique, le protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026 et les préalables que les syndicats estiment indispensables à l’organisation d’un concours et à une rentrée scolaire apaisée. Le secrétaire général du SNE, Michel Pépé Balamou, a d’abord tenu à clarifier la position de l’Intersyndicale sur le principe d’un concours. « L’Intersyndicale que vous voyez n’est pas opposée à l’organisation d’un concours. Il faut que cela soit très clair. Parce que c’est ce qui se dit actuellement dans la cité : “Les syndicalistes veulent que n’importe qui soit en classe pour enseigner nos enfants, ils s’opposent au concours”. Non ! Ni le SLECG, ni la FSPE, ni le SNE, personne n’est opposé à ce que les meilleurs soient recrutés pour enseigner dans les écoles de la République », a-t-il déclaré. Selon le responsable syndical, l’exigence de l’Intersyndicale porte avant tout sur le respect du protocole d’accord conclu avec le gouvernement. 4 500 enseignants ayant la moyenne revendiqués Michel Pépé Balamou rappelle qu’en 2024, 14 500 enseignants contractuels communaux avaient été identifiés, recensés, biométrisés puis soumis à une évaluation en pratique de classe. À l’issue de cette évaluation, 10 000 enseignants ont été retenus et 4 500 recalés, selon les chiffres avancés par le secrétaire général du SNE. Il précise toutefois que la majorité des 4 500 candidats recalés auraient obtenu la moyenne. « Parmi ces 4 500, seuls 60 n’ont pas eu la moyenne (…) Tout le reste, plus de 4 400 personnes ont obtenu une moyenne égale ou supérieure à 10/20. Cela signifie qu’ils ont le niveau », a-t-il soutenu. Pour le syndicaliste, le protocole d’accord leur accorde une priorité à l’engagement. « Le français est très clair : prioritaires à l’engagement. Qu’est-ce que cela signifie ? Cela implique que nous devions prendre leur moyenne : tous ceux qui ont entre 10 et 20/20 n’ont plus de concours à passer », a-t-il affirmé. Il estime donc que les enseignants contractuels de la zone spéciale de Conakry devraient, eux, être soumis à une évaluation en pratique de classe, conformément au protocole. Des retards dans l’application du protocole L’Intersyndicale reconnaît que certaines dispositions financières du protocole ont été appliquées. « En fin de septembre, 1 200 000 GNF doivent être ajoutés à la prime de documentation (pour la porter à 1 500 000 GNF), et 200 000 GNF restent au titre des indemnités de logement et de transport. C’est donc 1 400 000 GNF qui doivent être intégrés au salaire de tous les enseignants de Guinée à la fin de ce mois. Sur ce volet financier, le protocole est respecté », a expliqué Michel Pépé Balamou. En revanche, il déplore le retard accusé dans la mise en œuvre de plusieurs dispositions techniques. Selon lui, le protocole signé le 3 janvier 2026 prévoyait notamment la mise en place, dès février, de plusieurs commissions techniques. Celles-ci n’auraient finalement été installées qu’en avril, après des menaces syndicales. Trois commissions sont notamment concernées : celle chargée des enseignants contractuels communaux non retenus à l’issue des évaluations, celle chargée des actes de nomination des cadres devant bénéficier des primes de fonction et celle consacrée à la révision du statut particulier des personnels de l’éducation et de la formation. L’Intersyndicale fixe ses préalables Pour l’Intersyndicale, plusieurs engagements doivent être satisfaits avant l’organisation de tout concours au niveau du ministère de l’Éducation nationale. Elle réclame notamment : l’engagement des 4 500 enseignants contractuels communaux ayant obtenu la moyenne ; l’engagement des près de 2 000 enseignants contractuels de Conakry ; le paiement des 9 mois d’arriérés de salaire des 10 000 enseignants des collectivités ; la régularisation des situations administratives, notamment les échelons, indices et reclassements ; la régularisation des primes d’incitation, particulièrement en zone rurale ; l’amélioration des conditions matérielles et financières dans les établissements scolaires, notamment les écoles délabrées, le manque de latrines, d’eau, de tables-bancs, de matériel didactique et de cahiers. « Nous n’accepterons aucun principe d’organisation de concours au niveau du Ministère de l’Éducation nationale. L’Intersyndicale reste catégorique et formelle : tant que les points susmentionnés et clairement identifiés dans le protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026 ne sont pas satisfaits, il n’y aura pas de possibilité d’aboutir à une ouverture apaisée des classes », a conclu Michel Pépé Balamou. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Rentrée scolaire 2026 : l’Intersyndicale de l’éducation pose ses conditions avant tout recrutement est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Lutte TV Awards 2026 : le ministère des Sports dément tout « manque de considération » et pointe une invitation informelle
items.description: Deux jours après la cérémonie des Lutte TV Awards, le ministère de la Jeunesse et des Sports répond aux critiques sur l'absence de sa ministre. Dans une « mise au point » publiée ce lundi 21 septembre 2026, il affirme n'avoir reçu aucune invitation officielle et renvoie la responsabilité aux organisateurs. La cérémonie s'est tenue le samedi 19 septembre au NOOM Hôtel de Dakar. L'absence de la ministre y avait suscité des critiques, certaines dénonçant un désintérêt pour le monde de la lutte. Le ministère y répond en évoquant des « allégations publiques » et « un prétendu manque de considération envers le secteur de la lutte ». « Aucune invitation officielle » Le ministère est catégorique : la ministre « n'a reçu aucune invitation officielle à cet événement par les voies institutionnelles ». Il va plus loin en citant les organisateurs, qui auraient « eux-mêmes reconnu n'avoir sollicité le Ministère qu'à 48 heures de la cérémonie, par un canal informel ». Selon le communiqué, ce contact tardif s'expliquait par « les incertitudes qui pesaient sur la tenue de l'événement ». Le ministère en tire la conclusion suivante : « aucune participation ne pouvait raisonnablement être programmée ». Un rappel au « cadre de gouvernance du sport » Le texte prend ensuite un ton plus ferme. Le ministère rappelle « l'exigence du respect du cadre de gouvernance du sport, notamment dans leurs rapports avec l'administration ». Il lance aussi « un appel à la responsabilité dans les prises de parole publiques, surtout de la part de personnes citées en modèle », sans désigner nommément qui que ce soit. Le département assure qu'il « s’emploie au développement de toutes les disciplines sportives, sans distinction » et « réaffirme son engagement constant aux côtés de la lutte, sport national et patrimoine de notre pays ». Il conclut que « les manquements des acteurs ne sauraient être couverts par la désinformation et la manipulation ». O.B.N

However, the Tottenham Hotspur midfielder communicated his decision to withdraw from squad with his place being taken by Mohammed Fuseini. Speaking at Monday afternoon’s press conference, the Portuguese trainer said the player needed more time to recover fully after his engagement against Aston Villa. “It is simple for you guys to understand. items.title: After Aleema, Imran’s sisters Uzma and Noreen also detained in Lahore under MPO for 30 days
items.description: Former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan’s sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were detained for 30 days on Monday, ahead of the party’s September 27 protest call. The development follows the detention of Imran’s other sister, Aleema Khan, after Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days on Sunday. The detention has come amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. In an order dated Sept 20, a copy of which is available with Dawn , the Lahore DC Office ordered that Noreen and Uzma be detained for 30 days under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960, stating that the two were “prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”. The MPO ordinance allows the authorities to order detention and restrict judicial review of such orders. The two will remain in custody under the superintendent, Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat, it said. The order stated that the two were involved in the May 9 protest and “motivated the workers to damage public and government property”. “Moreover, they are again mobilising the workers through social media and public meetings to create a law and order situation, raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the government/institution in order to provoke and incite them,” the order read. “Accordingly, multiple cases including 96/23 PS Race Course were registered,” it said, stating that Uzma and Noreen were “potential dangers to public peace and tranquillity”. “Such activists will give rise to a situation prejudicial to public safety and maintenance of public order, if left unchecked.” The decision was taken in a meeting held on Sunday, under the chairmanship of the Lahore DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz, where the issue was discussed and members “endorsed” the “evidence” presented by the police. The order stated that the Lahore DC was convinced that Uzma and Noreen’s presence “at any public place will pose a grave threat to the public safety and will likely cause breach of public peace and public order”. In a post on X in the early hours of Monday, the party’s Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram had accused Punjab police of “arresting both sisters of Imran, along with their children and the sons of Aleema Khan”. Akram claimed that the individuals had “been placed in an armoured vehicle and are being taken to an unknown location”. PTI lawyer Awais Younas Chaudhry had confirmed to Dawn that all three of Imran’s sisters had been arrested. “Earlier Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were confined to their house, but on Monday morning they were taken to an unknown place,” he claimed. PTI, in a post on X, condemned the alleged arrest, calling it a “blatant abuse of authority, a violation of fundamental rights, and an act of political victimisation”. “Such conduct is illegal, unconstitutional, and is condemned in the strongest possible terms,” the party said. Meanwhile, Imran’s son Kasim Khan, in a post on X, alleged that Uzma and Noreen had been “abducted”. “This is a disgrace,” Kasim wrote, claiming that authorities had “broken into my aunties and cousins houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation”. “No reasons for arrest have been stated. No news has been released as to where they have been taken,” he wrote. PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, in a post on X, condemned the detention and stressed that the country did not “need further confrontation, rather an end to political tensions”. Gohar noted that the arrest of “PTI’s parliamentarians and their family members will only exacerbate tensions”. “The state must immediately alter its course of action. We are merely seeking justice and raising our voices for it,” he wrote. Speaking to Dawn , former member of the Punjab Assembly Seemabia Tahir said, “It was unfortunate that the family members [..] were facing such brutality”. She expressed hope that following this, “people will surely come out of their houses on Sept 27”. Aleema’s detention On Sunday, Aleema was detained under similar orders. The September 20 order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said DC Ijaz had ordered the detention or arrest of Aleema and a man named Muhammad Ameer under the Punjab MPO. Following the arrest, Aleema’s sister Noreen addressed a press conference in Lahore, flanked by her sister’s counsel, Advocate Mudassir Umar. Noreen claimed Aleema was “picked up” along with her driver after she left her residence on Saturday, and they later learnt that Aleema’s vehicle was parked at a police station. Meanwhile, the lawyer said they had yet to receive official confirmation of her arrest. Police sources had confirmed to Dawn on Sunday that Aleema was taken to Lahore’s Kot Lakhpat jail. After Uzma and Noreen were also detained, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja posted on X that in light of “fascist onslaught” in Punjab, particularly Lahore, an organising committee had been formed for the Lahore district to run the party’s matter “through consultation and agreement”. He added that consultations would be held with parliamentarians in Punjab on Monday and Tuesday. He also shared a statement notifying the constitution of the committee. The statement said, ““The organising committee shall have complete authority to take all actions and devise and implement all plans for the better functioning of the affairs of the party in the Lahore district.” Former lawmaker Malik Zaheer Abbas has been appointed as the committee’s convener and the body also compises Haroon Akbar, Asghar Gujjar, Awais Anjum, Yasir Gillani and Amir Qureshi. Even more detentions The detentions of Imran’s sisters come after a string of reported actions against the PTI in Punjab and Islamabad ahead of its September 27 protest. PTI Chairman Gohar claims that around 1,500 party workers have been arrested so far. “Five of our MNAs have been arrested, along with an ex-senator. Our MPAs have been arrested; one of them was arrested in Islamabad. Even our ministers are being arrested in our own province,” he alleged during a press conference in Peshawar. Speaking alongside him, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi claimed that men in plain clothes had “attacked and abducted” KP Labour Minister Fazal Shakoor. He also mentioned the reported attempt to “kidnap” the provincial minister for communications, Shakeel Khan in Batkhela. But, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the allegations were “a complete lie”. Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, he questioned, “Who can abduct a provincial minister in a provincial capital, which they (the PTI) govern?” In the rest of the press briefing, Afridi rued that his party had been subjected to “force, oppression and fascism” since April 9, 2022 — when Imran was ousted as the prime minister through a no-confidence vote. He held the country’s rulers responsible for reported deaths during these actions against his party. The KP CM reiterated that all three of Imran’s sisters and children as young as six years old had been “abducted”. “Nonetheless, PTI is still the most popular political party of Pakistan and Imran Khan is the most popular leader,” he remarked. CM Afridi reiterated that peaceful protest was the right of a political party, guaranteed under the Constitution and law, adding that the PTI had decided in its parliamentary party meeting earlier in the day to go ahead with its plan for a protest on Sept 27. He further announced that the party would share a detailed plan for the planned long march on September 25. For his part, Gohar said the “situation would improve if we seriously listen to each other, rather than threaten each other” and urged the state to “change its ways”. He also expressed the resolve to go ahead with the planned march on Sept 27, assuring the the PTI would not take the law into its hands. On Sunday, Sahiwal police arrested Asad Khan Baloch, former mayor of the municipal corporation and ex-ticket holder for PTI, along with the party’s city president in Sahiwal, Muhammad Shahid Chohan. PTI also claimed that MNAs Sanaullah Mastikhel , Ahsan Jamal Khan and Mian Ghous were taken into custody, according to the party’s information secretary. District authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under MPO a week ago, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh. Similar reports have come from Islamabad, where the PTI plans to march on the protest day. However, the government has vowed to stop the march, and the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”. ‘Flagrant violation of rights’ Condemning the reported detentions, the Amnesty International said in a statement that “the targeting of Imran Khan’s family and PTI party activists is a flagrant violation of their rights to liberty, freedom of expression, association and peaceful assembly”. “Such actions speak to the severity of the current restrictions in Pakistan,” it added. Amnesty noted that the “pre-emptive arrests of PTI members come ahead of planned country-wide protests by the party on Sept 27, which government officials have openly vowed to stop”. “Roadblocks are already being erected in Islamabad.” These developments did not bid well, especially given the authorities’ “long track record of reckless and unlawful use of force against protesters,” the statement read. “A protest cannot be deemed violent before it has even started. Pakistan’s authorities must uphold their obligations under international human rights law to facilitate peaceful assembly and refrain from unlawful measures to thwart these protests,” Amnesty urged.

items.title: Sammy Gyamfi backs Mahama’s directive to restore NACOC’s at ports
items.description: GoldBod Chief Executive Officer, Sammy Gyamfi, has welcomed President John Dramani Mahama’s reported directive to restore the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to Ghana’s list of Port Inspection Agencies following a recent drug trafficking incident linked to one of the country’s ports. Mr Gyamfi said the development was a matter of concern to patriotic Ghanaians, arguing that the incident raised questions about the effectiveness of monitoring and inspection systems at Ghana’s ports. “Clearly, these incidents could have only been occasioned by weak monitoring and inspection systems at our ports,” he said. According to him, NACOC, which is mandated to monitor, regulate, enforce and control narcotics trafficking, was removed from the list of Port Inspection Agencies by the government in June 2018. “While it is unclear what may have informed that decision in 2018, it is evident that the said decision weakened NACOC’s port inspection function,” Mr Gyamfi said. He said the reported decision by President Mahama to restore NACOC to the inspection regime was a welcome development. “It is therefore refreshing to learn that President Mahama has directed that effective immediately, NACOC be restored to the list of Port Inspection Agencies and granted unfettered access to all entry and exit points; by air, land and sea,” he stated. Mr Gyamfi also said he understood that the President had directed that all scanners and personnel at Ghana’s ports be changed with immediate effect. “I believe that these measures, if implemented effectively, will strengthen checks and control at our ports to forestall the reccurrence of these unfortunate incidents,” he added.

items.title: Première inculpation au Royaume-Uni d’un homme soupçonné d’implication dans le génocide au Rwanda
items.description: Un homme de 65 ans, Vincent Brown, également connu sous le nom de Vincent Bajinya, a été arrêté et inculpé lundi au Royaume-Uni, soupçonné d'avoir participé au génocide de 1994 au Rwanda, ont annoncé la police et les services du procureur, précisant qu'il s'agissait d'une première inculpation dans le pays pour ces faits. Cet homme, originaire de Kigali et résidant à Londres, a été arrêté à l'issue d'une enquête de sept ans. « Il est soupçonné d'avoir dirigé et incité à commettre des actes de meurtre et de génocide perpétrés par d'autres personnes », a déclaré le procureur Frank Ferguson dans un communiqué. Plus de 800.000 personnes selon l'ONU, essentiellement des membres de la minorité tutsi, ont été tuées au printemps 1994 dans des massacres orchestrés par des extrémistes hutu après la mort du président Juvénal Habyarimana dans un attentat contre son avion. AFP

items.title: Bas-Mono : Le collège des notables installé à Attitogon
items.description: Afagnan, 21 sept. (ATOP) – Le collège des notables du canton d’Attitogon, chef-lieu de la commune Bas-Mono 2, a été installé, le samedi 19 septembre dans la localité. La cérémonie s’est déroulée sous la présidence du chef canton, Togbui Yaovi Kouakou Assiatahoun VIII. Le collège est constitué de 16 personnes ressources des quartiers, reconnues pour leur sagesse, engagement, responsabilité et participation aux travaux communautaires. Il a pour mission d’accompagner le chef canton dans sa mission, de rassembler les populations des quartiers autour des idéaux de paix et de cohésion sociale. Il a également pour rôle de coordonner les actions dans les quartiers et de travailler de concert avec le chef canton pour le développement socio-économique, durable et harmonieux du canton. La cérémonie a été marquée par la remise des chapes et des attestations aux récipiendaires. Togbui Yaovi Kouakou Assiatahoun VIII a rappelé que la mise en place du collège des notables répond à la volonté de rapprocher la chefferie traditionnelle de la base et de rendre plus efficace l’action communautaire. Il a invité les notables à faire preuve de disponibilité, d’impartialité et de sens de l’écoute. Togbui Assiatahoun VIII a exhorté les comités de développement à la base à travailler en collaboration avec les notables, tout en favorisant le vivre ensemble, unité et la cohésion sociale pour le développement inclusif du milieu. Les notables ont exprimé leur gratitude au chef canton pour la confiance placée en eux. Ils ont pris l’engagement de servir loyalement Attitogon en se mettant au service de toute la population. ATOP/DK/SED

items.title: Queiroz provides insight into Kudus’ decision to withdraw from Black Stars squad
items.description: Black Stars head coach Carlos Queiroz has provided insight into Mohammed Kudus’ decision to withdraw from Ghana’s squad for the upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. The 26-year-old was initially named in Ghana’s squad for the qualifiers against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia but withdrew on Sunday after featuring for Tottenham Hotspur in their Premier League clash with Aston Villa. Queiroz revealed that his initial discussions with Kudus had been positive, but the situation changed after the forward featured for his club. The Portuguese coach also acknowledged that national team coaches do not have full control over decisions concerning players at club level. “It is simple for you guys to understand. In the course of our decisions as national team coaches, we cannot control the decisions of club coaches. “In the course of our conversations, it looked like Kudus was moving in the right direction. After playing 70-something minutes for Tottenham, we had a little conversation with him and decided it would be best for him to rest and recover properly. “We have to make decisions based on the information we have in our hands,” Queiroz said. Kudus’ withdrawal means he will miss Ghana’s opening two AFCON 2027 qualifying fixtures against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia.

items.title: Restauration de la mangrove ; le maire de Djirnda plaide pour une protection des îles du Saloum contre le changement climatique
items.description: Ndindé, un hameau de la commune de Djirnda, dans les îles du Saloum (Foundiougne), a vibré dimanche au rythme d'une journée de restauration de la mangrove initiée par l'ONG ActionAid. Cette activité a permis à Badara Diome, maire de Djirnda, d'anticiper sur la Conférence des parties sur les changements climatiques (Cop 31 du 9 au 20 novembre 2026 à Antalya en Turquie) et d'appeler également l'État à mettre en place un Plan spécial de protection insulaire. FOUNDIOUGNE – Tous, arborant des tee-shirt verts, plusieurs dizaines de jeunes ont pris part hier à la restauration de la mangrove de Ndindé, un hameau de la commune de Djirnda, dans les îles du Saloum (Foundiougne). Initiée par l'ONG ActionAid à travers la campagne “Fund Our Future” (Financer notre avenir), cette activité de reboisement a vu la présence de Badara Diome, maire de Djirnda, de l'adjoint au sous-préfet de Niodior, Mamadou Diagne, entre autres autorités. De nombreuses propagules ont été plantées sur un espace de 5 hectares. À travers cette action, les initiateurs entendent densifier la mangrove qui subit les effets du changement climatique. D'une façon générale, il s'agit de s'ériger en défenseur de l'environnement et particulièrement du domaine agroécologique. “Le message que nous portons à travers cette campagne est qu'il y ait, au moins, une augmentation de 30% du budget réservé à l'agroécologie”, à laissé entendre Rodolphe Aguemon, chargé de communication et de campagne à ActionAid. A lire aussi : Construire en milieu insulaire : quand l’eau devient un facteur bloquant La journée a été surtout un prétexte pour anticiper sur la Conférence des parties sur les changements climatiques (Cop 31 du 9 au 20 novembre 2026 à Antalya en Turquie). Pour le maire de Djirnda, cet événement de grande envergure doit être une occasion pour les hautes autorités du pays d'enfiler la robe d'avocat pour le milieu insulaire menacé par le changement climatique. “En tant qu’insulaires, nous sommes menacés par l'avancée de la mer, l'érosion côtière, la dégradation des habitats et de la biodiversité, par la diminution de la mangrove, la perte des surfaces cultivables…L’État du Sénégal doit porter le plaidoyer en faveur de la protection insulaire pour que nos villages soient à l'abri”, alerte l'autorité locale. Mieux, l'édile de Djirnda va plus loin pour proposer une stratégie de préservation de ces localités exposées aux risques environnementaux. De l'avis de Badara Diome, l'État doit élaborer un Plan spécial pour les îles du Saloum. C'est ce qu'il éclaircit ici :“L'État, en collaboration avec les collectivités locales et les partenaires au développement, doit mettre en place un document ayant trait à la protection des îles et à leur développement”. D'ici là, les populations poursuivent la lutte de protection de leurs terroirs à travers des initiatives locales comme cette séance de restauration de la mangrove du hameau de Ndindé. Selon les témoignages d'experts, la mangrove participe activement à la protection des communautés. En plus d'être un habitat naturel pour les poissons et les oiseaux, elle assure aussi la séquestration du carbone. D'ailleurs, au sujet de ce dernier, le maire de Djirnda a porté à la connaissance du public de l'existence du projet de Crédit carbone du Delta du Saloum. “On espère pouvoir commencer à recevoir les redevances du crédit carbone d'ici 2027”, informe Badara Diome. El hadji Fodé SARR (Correspondant)

items.title: Zoundwéogo/Gogo: la veille citoyenne réaffirme son soutien à la RPP
items.description: BURKINA-ZOUNDWÉOGO-GOGO-RPP-VEILLE-CITOYENNE Zoundwéogo/Gogo: la veille citoyenne réaffirme son soutien à la RPP Gogo, 19 sept. 2026 (AIB)- La veille citoyenne de Gogo a réaffirmé, samedi, son soutien à la Révolution populaire et progressiste (RPP) et au Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, à l’occasion de l’inauguration du 133e rond-point réalisé dans la commune. La cérémonie a réuni notamment le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Gogo, Issa Tiendrebeogo, des chargés de mission des régions du Nazinon et de l’Oubri, le Nabikinga de Gogo ainsi que plusieurs représentants des forces vives de la commune. Le Nabikinga de Gogo a salué l’initiative de la veille citoyenne, estimant que l’infrastructure constitue un symbole de mobilisation et de maintien de la veille citoyenne. Il a appelé les filles et fils de Gogo à renforcer leur engagement en faveur des actions de développement et des initiatives nationales. Le président de la coopérative AES Lagmtaaba et initiateur de la cérémonie, Alassane Dipama, a indiqué que ce rond-point est le 133e réalisé dans la commune. « Cette forte mobilisation démontre que la RPP est bien en marche ici à Gogo. Notre soutien, depuis les premières heures de la Révolution, est sans faille. Nous sommes avec le camarade capitaine nuit et jour », a-t-il déclaré. Le camarade Dipama a également fait savoir que la coopérative a contribué à la formation de 600 femmes à la confection du pagne Koko Donda, dans le cadre de ses actions en faveur de leur autonomisation économique. Pour le chargé de mission auprès de la Présidence du Faso pour la région du Nazinon, le camarade Wendpasamdé Thierry Nikiema, chaque citoyen doit faire preuve d’engagement et de responsabilité. Il a invité les citoyens à privilégier l’humilité, le travail et la quête du savoir, estimant que la réussite de la dynamique nationale repose sur la participation et l’accompagnement responsable de tous. Le PDS de Gogo, Issa Tiendrebeogo, a, pour sa part, exhorté la jeunesse à s’approprier les initiatives de développement et à participer activement à la construction de la commune et du pays. Il a particulièrement appelé les jeunes à accompagner les initiatives présidentielles, dont plusieurs, a-t-il relevé, concernent directement cette frange de la population. La cérémonie s’est achevée par la coupure officielle du ruban et l’inauguration du 133e rond-point de la commune de Gogo. Agence d’Information du Burkina KP/BGB/bak

items.title: El Gobierno reprocha el “exceso” del Supremo con la ‘ley de nietos’: “No existe ningún riesgo derivado del crecimiento del censo”
items.description: La Abogacía del Estado considera que la decisión del Tribunal Supremo de suspender el derecho al voto de los nacionalizados por la ley de nietos supone un “exceso” por parte de los jueces, a quienes reprochan estar cuestionando la legalidad de una instrucción del Ministerio de Justicia que nadie ha impugnado ante el alto tribunal. Así lo exponen los servicios jurídicos del Gobierno en el recurso que han presentado contra las dos resoluciones con las que el Supremo justificó la paralización cautelar de la inscripción en el censo electoral de los beneficiarios de la Ley de Memoria Democrática en la existencia de “un peligro fundado, real y serio de poder afectar gravemente a la objetividad y transparencia del proceso electoral”. “No existe ningún riesgo derivado del crecimiento del censo (...). Y aun en el negado caso de que existiese algún riesgo, sería tan ínfimo que no justificaría cercenar los derechos de voto de cientos de miles de personas, piedra angular de la democracia”, señala la Abogacía, que recuerda que “nadie puede predecir el sentido del voto” de los nacionalizados y que, en cualquier caso, este “no podría alterar el resultado electoral por pura matemática”. items.title: Entretiens mauritano-espagnol à Nouakchott autour de la coopération bilatérale entre les deux pays
items.description: Le ministre des Affaires économiques et du Développement, Abdallahi Ould Souleimane Ould Cheikh Sidiya, a examiné ce lundi, avec l'ambassadeur d'Espagne en Mauritanie, Pablo Barbara Gómez, les différents aspects de la coopération économique entre les deux pays et les moyens de développer leur partenariat en matière de développement. Le ministère des Affaires économiques a indiqué dans un communiqué que la rencontre avait porté sur les mécanismes de renforcement du partenariat entre la Mauritanie et l’Espagne et le soutien aux programmes de transition économique et de gouvernance du développement. Elle a également permis de faire le point sur l’avancement de la mise en œuvre des programmes de coopération technique et financière proposés par l’Espagne à la Mauritanie. Les deux parties ont réaffirmé leur volonté de poursuivre la coordination et la concertation concernant les relations entre les deux pays, et de développer leur coopération au service du développement et de la stabilité dans la région.
